title: Claude-assisted discovery of an Apache ActiveMQ Classic code-injection flaw
summary: Horizon3.ai reports a remote code execution flaw in ActiveMQ Classic, introduced about 13 years earlier, that chains the Jolokia management API with network-connector VM transports. Apache rates it important and fixes it in 5.19.4 and 6.2.3.
ai_role: The finder, Naveen Sunkavally, says Claude did a first-pass source analysis and traced the exploit path, and describes the work as 80% Claude with human prompting, a test target and reporting. Apache credits him as finder.
classification_note: The cited sources establish an AI-assisted finding and a coordinated report to Apache on 22 March 2026. They do not establish a zero-day incident; exploitation reports are not assessed here.
remediation_note: Apache's announcement lists 5.19.4 and 6.2.3 as fixed releases; the Horizon3 post cites later releases in its timeline, so check the vendor for the current fixed version. Deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: An authenticated attacker can invoke Jolokia MBean connector operations on an affected ActiveMQ Classic broker.
impacts.exploitation: CISA ADP records active exploitation and a KEV addition on 2026-04-16.

title: Claude finds a FreeBSD RPCSEC_GSS kernel stack overflow
summary: FreeBSD advisory SA-26:08 describes a stack overflow in the RPCSEC_GSS code that can allow remote code execution in the kernel, with no workaround, affecting all supported versions. It credits Nicholas Carlini using Claude, Anthropic.
ai_role: The advisory credits Claude. Anthropic's report says Claude Mythos Preview found the bug and wrote a working exploit with no human involvement after the initial request; that autonomy claim is Anthropic's own and the advisory does not name the model.
classification_note: The advisory establishes the AI-credited finding and fixes. Neither source establishes that the flaw was exploited in the wild, and the autonomy claim is not independently verified.
remediation_note: The advisory lists corrected releases dated 26 March 2026, including 15.0-RELEASE-p5, 14.4-RELEASE-p1, 14.3-RELEASE-p10 and 13.5-RELEASE-p11. Deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: RPCSEC_GSS must be reachable: the CNA describes kernel NFS with kgssapi.ko loaded, or a userspace RPC server using librpcgss_sec. Its initial paragraph says packet validation does not require authentication, while its kernel-impact paragraph specifies an authenticated user; this distinction is unresolved.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the CNA description; CISA ADP records a proof of concept, not observed exploitation.

title: Hacktron's AI agent finds a BeyondTrust remote-support command injection
product: BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access
summary: Hacktron reports an OS command injection in BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access, rated critical with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.9 and a variant of CVE-2024-12356 on the same WebSocket endpoint. BeyondTrust published advisory BT26-02 on 6 February 2026.
ai_role: Hacktron says its agents found the flaw through AI-enabled variant analysis during autonomous scans; the post does not detail the human review beyond the team's validation and disclosure.
classification_note: Hacktron's timeline shows a report on 31 January 2026 and a patch before public disclosure. The sources do not establish that the flaw was unknown to attackers beforehand.
remediation_note: Hacktron reports patches for cloud and on-premises deployments (Remote Support 25.3.2 and later; Privileged Remote Access 25.1.1 and later). The BeyondTrust advisory page returned HTTP 403 and was not read; deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: An unauthenticated remote attacker can send crafted requests to affected BeyondTrust RS or PRA versions; commands run as the site user.
impacts.exploitation: CISA ADP records active exploitation and a KEV addition on 2026-02-13.

title: Big Sleep identifies an undisclosed SQLite vulnerability
organization: Google Project Zero, Google DeepMind and Google Threat Intelligence
summary: Google reports that Big Sleep, guided by threat intelligence, identified CVE-2025-6965 while the flaw was known to threat actors and at risk of exploitation. Google says its intervention prevented the anticipated use; this is not evidence of an observed successful hack.
ai_role: An AI agent combined code analysis with indicators supplied by human threat-intelligence researchers.
classification_note: Google describes a flaw known only to threat actors before its intervention. This is attributed zero-day context, not an independent finding of active exploitation.
remediation_note: SQLite records a fix on 27 June 2025 and lists release 3.50.2, dated 28 June 2025. The later Google post describes the AI contribution, not the patch date.

impacts.exploitation: Observed exploitation is not established by the CNA description; CISA ADP records a proof of concept.

title: o3 helps find a Linux kernel ksmbd use-after-free
summary: Independent researcher Sean Heelan reports a use-after-free of sess->user in the ksmbd session-logoff handler, reachable when a second connection binds to the same session. The fix removes the free in smb2pdu.c and is tagged for stable backporting.
ai_role: Heelan ran o3 through the API 100 times on about 12k lines of SMB handler code, with no scaffolding or tools. o3 reported the bug in some runs with a signal-to-noise ratio he puts near 1:50, and he identified the real finding himself and wrote the patch.
classification_note: Per the author's account the bug was not previously known to him; the source does not independently show it was unknown to others.
remediation_note: The kernel commit 2fc9feff45d9 (ksmbd: fix use-after-free in session logoff) authored by Heelan removes the faulty free. The kernel release containing it was not established here.

scenarios:
AV:N - ksmbd is the in-kernel SMB server; both the freeing SMB2 LOGOFF and the racing SMB2 SESSION_SETUP (multichannel bind) are ordinary SMB PDUs delivered over TCP/445 from a remote client. No local access is required.
AC:L - The attacker controls both sides of the race — they open both TCP connections and choose when to send LOGOFF and the binding SESSION_SETUP — and both paths block on slow ksmbd.mountd IPC round trips (`ksmbd_ipc_login_request()` / `ksmbd_ipc_logout_request()`), giving a very wide window that can be retried indefinitely with fresh sessions.
PR:L - `smb2_session_logoff()` is gated by `ksmbd_conn_good()` and a successful `ksmbd_session_lookup_all()`, and channel binding requires a non-guest session, so the attacker needs one ordinary unprivileged SMB account (any share user, no admin rights) — matching the kernel CNA scoring of the sibling multichannel session UAFs CVE-2025-22040/22041.
UI:N - The attacker drives both connections and both SMB requests entirely on their own; no action by any local user or administrator is needed.
S:U - The corruption stays within the kernel's own memory and security authority — a standard in-kernel use-after-free with no crossing of a VM, IOMMU, or sandbox boundary.
C:H - The freed `struct ksmbd_user` holds `name`, `passkey` and `passkey_sz`; after reclaim, `ksmbd_compare_user()` performs a `memcmp` of attacker-chosen length through a dangling pointer (unbounded OOB read usable as an oracle) and `smb2_query_info` FS_OBJECTID copies 16 bytes via `user_passkey(sess->user)` straight into the network response, disclosing kernel memory and the victim's NTLM passkey to the remote client.
I:H - `set_user_flag(sess->user, KSMBD_USER_FLAG_BAD_PASSWORD)` performs an OR-write into the freed object, and `sess->user->uid`/`->gid` from freed memory drive `smb_inherit_dacl()` and file ownership; combined with heap spraying of the reclaimed slab object this yields a write primitive suitable for control-flow hijack.
A:H - Dereferencing the freed `ksmbd_user` (and the `sess->user = NULL` store racing other readers) reliably produces kernel oopses, slab corruption, or a panic, taking down the file server.

title: AI-generated fuzzing reveals an OpenSSL memory-access flaw
organization: Google Open Source Security Team and OpenSSL
summary: An AI-generated fuzz target revealed an issue in low-level elliptic-curve handling. OpenSSL rates it low severity because vulnerable application use is considered unlikely and the problematic inputs do not arise in ordinary X.509 certificate processing.
ai_role: Google attributes the finding to LLM-generated fuzz targets; OpenSSL credits Google OSS-Fuzz-Gen for the report.
classification_note: The sources document an AI-assisted discovery and public advisory. They do not establish a zero-day exploitation incident.
remediation_note: The 16 October advisory lists corrective commits and planned branch releases; it explicitly did not issue immediate new releases because severity was low. Patch availability is not the same as deployment to users.

impacts.conditions: An application must supply untrusted exotic explicit binary-curve parameters to the affected low-level APIs. OpenSSL considers vulnerable application use unlikely; ordinary X.509 inputs cannot represent the problematic values. Crashes are described and remote code execution is only a possibility that cannot be ruled out.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the cited CNA description; no independent exploitation assessment made.

title: Xint Code AI scan surfaces the Linux kernel Copy Fail flaw
organization: Theori (Xint Code Research Team; researcher Taeyang Lee)
summary: A logic bug in the Linux kernel authencesn cryptographic template. Per the Xint account, an unprivileged local user can cause a controlled write into the page cache of readable files, with privilege escalation reported on the four distributions tested (Ubuntu 24.04, Amazon Linux 2023, RHEL 10.1, SUSE 16). The on-disk file is not modified, so on-disk checksums may miss it. Impact claims are the researchers' own and were not independently verified here.
ai_role: Per Xint's account, Theori researcher Taeyang Lee began the work, and the finding was AI-assisted: Xint Code scanned the crypto subsystem from a short operator prompt in about an hour and ranked Copy Fail highest. Secure.com credits Lee's initial insight; Theori's press release emphasizes the tool more.
classification_note: Timeline from the Xint post: reported to the kernel security team 2026-03-23, mainline patch 2026-04-01, CVE assigned 2026-04-22, public disclosure 2026-04-29. A CISA KEV listing reported by one secondary source was not verified and is not used.
remediation_note: Patch committed to mainline 2026-04-01. Stable fixes listed by Mend as 6.18.22, 6.19.12 and 7.0 are from a secondary source and were not checked against kernel.org. Deployed patch status is not checked.

scenarios:
AV:L - The vulnerable algif_aead path is reached through local AF_ALG socket syscalls: socket, bind, setsockopt, accept, sendmsg, and recvmsg. It is not directly reachable from remote network packets.
AC:L - A local attacker can construct the AF_ALG AEAD request, choose buffer layout, AAD/tag lengths, and invoke recvmsg directly. Any race or SGL layout condition is attacker-controlled from the same process.
PR:L - Creating and using AF_ALG AEAD sockets requires only an unprivileged local user on systems with CRYPTO_USER_API_AEAD enabled. The traced socket, bind, setsockopt, accept, sendmsg, and recvmsg paths do not require CAP_SYS_ADMIN or other real root privileges.
UI:N - No victim interaction is needed once the attacker has local code execution. The attacker can open and drive the AF_ALG socket entirely through syscalls.
S:U - The issue remains within the kernel/user crypto API security authority and does not cross a VM, IOMMU, or separate sandbox boundary. This is a standard local kernel attack surface.
C:H - The removed in-place AEAD design used user-writable RX scatterlists as crypto source data and chained TX tag pages, creating a plausible decryption/authentication bypass for data protected by secret AEAD keys. Under the required uncertainty rule, this is scored as high confidentiality impact.
I:H - The bug undermines AEAD authenticity by allowing source data used by the crypto operation to diverge from the data originally submitted and authenticated. This can allow forged or corrupted plaintext/ciphertext results, so integrity impact is high.
A:H - The vulnerable path builds complex chained scatterlists from attacker-controlled local buffers and related AF_ALG fixes show these paths can lead to scatterwalk NULL dereferences and kernel panics. A local attacker can repeatedly trigger the operation, so availability impact is high.

title: GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent finds a Quarkus path-based authorization bypass
summary: GHSL reports an authorization bypass in Quarkus HTTP path-based security rules: access checks ran on the raw URL path, while routing removed matrix parameters before matching endpoints. Endpoints protected by @RolesAllowed or @Authenticated are not affected, per the advisory. Tested on 3.32.4; severity is not stated on the GHSL page.
ai_role: GHSL says the Taskflow Agent, an AI-based framework, found the issue; GHSL team members Peter Stöckli and Man Yue Mo manually verified it before reporting.
classification_note: The GHSL write-up and Quarkus advisory establish an AI-assisted finding and fix. They do not establish exploitation in the wild.
remediation_note: Quarkus fixed the issue and published advisory GHSA-rc95-pcm8-65v9 on 4 May 2026. The GHSL page does not name the fixed version; check the Quarkus advisory. Deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: An affected Quarkus application uses HTTP path-based authorization with RESTEasy Reactive routing. Semicolon matrix parameters can bypass authorization policies while reaching the protected endpoint; this is an authorization bypass, not a claim of bypassing credential validation.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the cited CNA description; no independent exploitation assessment made.

title: GitHub Security Lab Taskflow Agent finds Rocket.Chat authentication bypass and NoSQL injection

ai_role: GHSL says the Taskflow Agent found both issues; GHSL team members Peter Stöckli and Man Yue Mo manually verified them before reporting.
classification_note: The GHSL advisory establishes an AI-assisted finding and fixes. It does not establish exploitation in the wild.
remediation_note: GHSL reports the first fix for GHSL-2026-004 in 8.0.0 (12 January 2026) and the fix for GHSL-2026-005 in a release of 5 March 2026 covering other supported versions. Deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: An affected Rocket.Chat ddp-streamer account service is reachable and the target user has a password set and a known or guessable username; arbitrary passwords can allow account takeover.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the cited CNA description; no independent exploitation assessment made.

title: XBOW's autonomous agent finds a GnuTLS-only Exim use-after-free
summary: Exim's advisory EXIM-Security-2026-05-01.1 describes a remotely reachable use-after-free in the BDAT body parsing path, rated Critical with CVSS 9.8. It affects Exim 4.97 through 4.99.2 only in builds compiled with GnuTLS; OpenSSL builds are not affected. Fixed in 4.99.3; the advisory states there is no mitigation other than upgrading.
ai_role: The advisory credits Federico Kirschbaum of XBOW as finder. XBOW's write-up attributes the discovery to its autonomous agent; the extent of human review before reporting is not described in the sources read.
classification_note: The Exim advisory and XBOW write-up establish an AI-attributed finding and a fix. They do not establish exploitation in the wild. Secondary sources disagree on whether public exploit code exists; that is not asserted here.
remediation_note: Exim 4.99.3 is the documented fixed release for affected 4.97 to 4.99.2 builds. Deployed patch status is not checked.

impacts.conditions: Exim before 4.99.3 uses an affected GnuTLS configuration and CHUNKING transfer; an unauthenticated network attacker can trigger heap corruption that could allow arbitrary code execution.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the cited CNA description; no independent exploitation assessment made.

title: XBOW's autonomous agent finds critical Bing Images command-injection RCE

classification_note: Microsoft's advisory and NVD entry establish the CVE; the AI attribution rests on XBOW's own account and press reports. Sources give conflicting dates for the server-side fix. Exploitation is not asserted.
remediation_note: Microsoft states the Bing issues were fixed server-side, so no customer action is documented. The sources conflict on whether the fix preceded the 19 March or the 23 July 2026 date. The MSRC page was not read directly. The MSRC advisory page renders by script and was not read in text form; the fix status rests on the linked account.

title: WolfSSL SM2/SM3 certificate verification out-of-bounds read
summary: Out-of-bounds heap read during SM2/SM3 certificate signature verification can occur when a public key is shorter than 65 bytes; the vendor advisory limits exposure to builds with SM2 support. The GitHub advisory calls this an out-of-bounds read, while Anthropic’s CVD report title uses “heap-buffer-overflow”; the technical description is a read, not a write.

title: Jetty WebSocket reserved opcode bypasses size checks and forces huge allocation
summary: With auto-fragmentation enabled, a reserved WebSocket opcode bypasses frame-size checks and clamps; Jetty allocates memory for the unvalidated attacker-declared payload before rejecting the opcode, enabling remote memory exhaustion.
ai_role: Anthropic CVD finding explicitly attributes discovery to Claude Mythos Preview; Jetty advisory identifies the individual GHSA and affected behavior.
classification_note: Public disclosure is documented. The cited accounts describe a remote unauthenticated denial-of-service condition; they do not establish exploitation in the wild or zero-day status. Anthropic says static analysis identified the bug and reports no attached reproducer.
remediation_note: The Jetty advisory lists patched releases 12.1.12, 12.0.38, 11.0.32, and 10.0.32.

title: libgit2 bundled PCRE heap buffer overflow

title: WAMR WASI poll_oneoff output buffer overflow
ai_system: Claude; Anthropic CVD snapshot identifies Claude Mythos Preview; the project advisory says Anthropic ran Claude Code, so the specific model/tool attribution differs by source.
summary: WAMR’s WASI poll_oneoff path fails to validate the output buffer for all events that may be written. A guest module can cause the host runtime to write an event past the allocated buffer, crossing the Wasm linear-memory boundary into adjacent host heap memory. The Anthropic CVD snapshot records repeatable ASan overflow findings; the project advisory and later release material identify the issue and fix. The attack requires execution of a malicious Wasm module in a WAMR host. Do not infer arbitrary code execution from the documented memory corruption.
ai_role: Anthropic CVD item explicitly attributes discovery to Claude Mythos Preview; WAMR’s advisory is the matching issue-level record.
classification_note: Project advisory GHSA-wj3p-xhqm-pffc was published Jul 16, 2026; Anthropic snapshot states public reveal on Aug 17, 2026. This date disagreement is retained here rather than resolved by using a later dashboard update date. WAMR 2.4.5 release notes identify CVE-2026-54914 and fix the poll_oneoff overflow. No exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: WAMR 2.4.5 release notes state that it fixes CVE-2026-54914. The Anthropic CVD snapshot includes the upstream bounds-check change and regression coverage. Deployment status is not checked.

title: Linux futex requeue can leave a waiter pointing into freed private hash memory
summary: A cross-process futex requeue can leave another process’s waiter pointing into a private futex hash table that is freed when its owner exits. Anthropic’s report presents the use-after-free and a possible local privilege-escalation chain; its suggested patch is explicitly described as LLM-authored and not reviewed beyond stopping the crash.
ai_role: The item-specific Anthropic CVD page explicitly says Claude discovered the vulnerability and Anthropic security triaged it. It records the limitation on the suggested patch.
classification_note: Anthropic publicly revealed this finding on August 18, 2026. The cited sources do not establish exploitation in the wild or zero-day status.
remediation_note: The Linux fix requires identical flags for sys_futex_requeue(); the kernel CVE notice links the fix commit. Anthropic cautions that the LLM-authored suggested patch in its report was not fully reviewed.

scenarios:
AV:L - The vulnerable code is reached through the local futex_requeue syscall path, not through network, adjacent, or physical input.
AC:L - An unprivileged attacker can create the needed futex waiters, choose mismatched source and destination flags, and control the requeue/lifetime sequence; any race or timing is attacker-controlled.
PR:L - The syscall has no capability or namespace gate, but the attacker needs basic local code execution to invoke futex syscalls and arrange the participating tasks.
UI:N - No victim action is required; the attacker can trigger the vulnerable futex operations from their own processes/threads.
S:U - The impact is within the kernel/local system security authority and is a standard local kernel memory corruption or privilege escalation scenario.
C:H - The bug is a kernel use-after-free caused by requeueing waiters across incompatible private/shared futex hash lifetimes, which can plausibly be shaped into kernel memory disclosure.
I:H - The use-after-free involves kernel heap/list/lock state reachable from attacker-controlled futex operations, making arbitrary kernel memory corruption or control-flow impact defensible.
A:H - Even without full exploitation, dereferencing and manipulating freed futex hash bucket state can crash or hang the kernel.

title: Linux epoll upward-depth walk can access a freed eventpoll object
summary: An epoll nesting-depth walker follows an eventpoll pointer while under RCU, but the pointed-to eventpoll object is freed without waiting for an RCU grace period. Anthropic describes the resulting use-after-free and a suggested kfree_rcu fix.
ai_role: The individual Anthropic CVD page explicitly credits Claude with discovery and Anthropic security with triage.
classification_note: The CVE record was published 2026-05-06.
remediation_note: The Anthropic report links the upstream kfree_rcu fix commit; Red Hat’s entry describes the same CVE and flaw but says Red Hat products are not affected.

scenarios:
AV:L - The vulnerable path is reached through local epoll syscalls, primarily `epoll_ctl(EPOLL_CTL_ADD)` on nested epoll descriptors racing with descriptor close/release. Network input is not sufficient to reach the lifetime bug without local control of epoll file descriptors.
AC:L - The race is attacker-controlled: an unprivileged local process can create the epoll graph and run concurrent threads performing nested `epoll_ctl()` and close/release operations. No rare external state or victim timing is required beyond winning a race the attacker can repeatedly drive.
PR:L - Creating epoll descriptors and calling `epoll_ctl()` require only ordinary local user privileges. No capability check gates the vulnerable nested epoll path; the only capability-related logic masks `EPOLLWAKEUP` and is not relevant.
UI:N - Exploitation does not require another user to open files, mount anything, or perform any action. The attacking process can create, nest, and close all relevant descriptors itself.
S:U - The impact is within the kernel security authority as a local kernel memory corruption or privilege escalation. There is no VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or cross-authority boundary change shown by this bug.
C:H - This is a use-after-free of `struct eventpoll` during an RCU walk, and the stale pointer can be dereferenced after the object is freed and potentially reallocated. Per kernel CVSS guidance, a UAF is treated as enabling high confidentiality impact through exploitable memory corruption.
I:H - The stale `struct eventpoll` is not only read but also written via fields such as `gen` and `loop_check_depth` after free, making heap corruption plausible if the memory is reallocated. Per kernel CVSS guidance, UAF memory corruption supports high integrity impact.
A:H - At minimum, dereferencing or writing a freed `struct eventpoll` can crash or corrupt the kernel. A local attacker can repeatedly trigger the race, so availability impact is high.

title: FreeRDP planar decoder bounds check uses the wrong stride

title: Outlook unsafe-action warning bypass can disclose NTLMv2 authentication data
summary: Microsoft says Outlook does not warn before opening a crafted message file causes a connection to an attacker-controlled network location, potentially disclosing the user’s NTLMv2 hash. Microsoft rates the issue moderate and reports exploitation detected.
ai_role: Microsoft’s acknowledgements credit Benoît Sevens “using Claude with Anthropic” for this CVE. This establishes Claude use by the credited researcher, but the advisory does not specify Claude’s exact discovery or validation contribution, nor the model version.

title: Rejetto HFS predictable session-signing key permits administrator-session forgery
summary: Horizon3 reports that Mythos identified how HFS’s predictable pseudo-random session-signing key and exposed generator outputs could be combined to forge an administrator session, enabling access to built-in server-side code execution. Horizon3’s verification agent confirmed the issue and demonstrated impact. The affected versions are 3.0.0 through 3.2.0.
ai_role: Horizon3 explicitly states that its cryptographic-weakness analysis agent, driven by Mythos, identified the linked signing-key and random-output disclosure issues. It says Mythos developed the proof of concept and demonstrated impact; a follow-up verification agent re-analyzed the code and confirmed the issue. The report describes Mythos as finding this vulnerability, not merely exploiting a known flaw.
classification_note: The CVE/GHSA and HFS 3.2.1 release were published 2026-07-13; Horizon3’s detailed Mythos attribution and analysis was published 2026-09-30. The researcher’s disclosure and attribution dates are kept separate. No claim about in-the-wild exploitation is included.
remediation_note: HFS 3.2.1 is the first fixed release linked from the CVE/GHSA record. The project release says previous versions contained security vulnerabilities and thanks Zach Hanley in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research. Upgrade to 3.2.1 or later.

title: curl may reuse a connection with mismatched STARTTLS configuration
summary: Project curl reports that an IMAP, POP3, SMTP, FTP, or LDAP transfer that upgrades from cleartext to TLS may incorrectly reuse a live connection even when the transfers’ TLS configurations differ. This can establish a connection with an unintended TLS configuration. Affected versions are curl 7.30.0 through 8.20.0; curl 8.21.0 fixes the issue.
ai_role: The upstream advisory credits Andrew Nesbitt as “powered by Mythos.” This directly attributes the report to AI-assisted discovery; it does not describe the exact division of work or model prompting.
classification_note: The curl advisory was published on 2026-06-24 and records the report date as 2026-05-06. The advisory says connection reuse can occur with mismatched TLS settings; this record makes no exploitation-in-the-wild or zero-day claim.
remediation_note: Project curl states that curl 8.21.0 fixes the issue and also provides fixed maintenance branches. The project recommends upgrading or applying the linked patch; it advises against cleartext-to-TLS transfers as a temporary mitigation.

title: wolfSSL (D)TLS 1.2 client accepts unauthenticated data after out-of-order ChangeCipherSpec
summary: A (D)TLS 1.2 client can accept an out-of-order ChangeCipherSpec before sending ClientKeyExchange and then accept attacker-supplied application data protected by a deterministic key. The vendor says DTLS 1.2 is exposed to out-of-order records; TLS 1.2 requires wolfSSL_inject() or read-ahead. Certificate suites require a man-in-the-middle position; PSK connections can be impersonated without knowing the PSK. Affected versions are 4.7.0 through 5.9.2.

The announcement quotes wolfSSL on results from 74 reports, including five CVEs, but does not map those five to CVE identifiers; model/version attribution for this individual case therefore remains unspecified.

The vendor says the issue affects TLS 1.0–1.3 and DTLS verification in either client or server roles. If the skipped certificate is an intermediate, it can be retained as a trusted signer in the context certificate manager. Exposure depends on both checks and the relevant build options.

title: wolfSSL session-cache references can resume a client connection as a different server

The process-global cache may then resolve the saved reference to another server’s session secrets, and resumption skips certificate and hostname checks. The vendor limits reachability to the legacy get_session/set_session flow and TLS/DTLS versions 1.2 and earlier; safer API flows and several build presets are not affected.

title: Rails safe_constantize can compile attacker-controlled regular expressions and crash the server
product: Ruby on Rails Active Support / Action Cable
summary: When constant lookup raises LoadError, safe_constantize compiles a regular expression from the requested constant name without escaping it. An application that passes untrusted input can allow crafted patterns to crash the server process. The advisory specifically identifies the default Action Cable channel subscription as an unauthenticated path; applications without that endpoint or with authentication checks have different exposure.
ai_role: The Rails advisory says the issue was also found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner, identified as ANT-2026-ZUN5KU3Q. It separately credits other researchers; the advisory does not describe the scanner model or its exact validation process.
classification_note: The maintainer published GHSA-8474-xrp6-wh69 on 2026-11-04 and lists CVE-2026-126080. This record makes no exploitation-in-the-wild or zero-day claim.
remediation_note: The advisory lists Active Support 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 as patched and supplies patches. It offers disabling the Action Cable mount or requiring authentication as mitigations; the latter limits but does not remove exposure if authenticated users can reach the path.

title: Rails Active Storage NUL-byte filenames can cause persistent denial of service
summary: Active Storage stores client-supplied filenames verbatim. On SQLite and MySQL/MariaDB, a permitted uploader can persist a filename containing a NUL byte; calls to File.basename or File.extname then raise ArgumentError when variants, previews or attachments are rendered, potentially disabling affected pages until the filename is purged or corrected. PostgreSQL rejects the row and is not affected.
ai_role: The Rails advisory directly says the issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner, identifier ANT-2026-UQM5Z4YL. The source does not identify the model or detail validation steps.
classification_note: The maintainer published GHSA-p2pm-g2h6-7j5j on 2026-11-04 and lists CVE-2026-126074. The advisory describes an availability vulnerability and does not assert exploitation.
remediation_note: The advisory lists Active Storage 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 as patched and provides patches. The persistent failure can also be cleared by purging the affected blob or correcting its filename; PostgreSQL rejects the problematic row.

title: Gitea Actions job tokens can make user commits appear signed by the instance
summary: A regular user who can run an Actions job can use its token to register an email and GPG key on the gitea-actions system account. Commit verification then presents that user’s commit as instance-signed and trusted, including in other users’ repositories. The advisory says the effect is on the displayed signer/trust level; it does not create signature validity or grant access, and signing-rule enforcement is unaffected.
ai_role: The Gitea maintainer advisory directly says the finding was reported by the Anthropic OSS scanner, identifier ANT-2026-VMTM4XVM. It does not identify a model.
classification_note: The maintainer published GHSA-mf6p-vqpw-3r7x on 2026-11-01 and lists CVE-2026-116474. The advisory demonstrates the behavior on a stock binary and marks severity moderate. It explicitly limits impact to displayed signer/trust status; this record makes no exploitation-in-the-wild claim.
remediation_note: The advisory lists Gitea 28.3.0 as patched. Its recommended remediation combines rejecting account-data writes from non-positive job-token IDs with verifier logic that skips keys whose owner does not exist. It notes that previously planted database rows may need cleanup.

title: Rails Action Controller Live can deadlock threads when closing a full response queue
product: Ruby on Rails Action Pack / Action Controller Live
summary: When a client stops reading and a bounded ActionController::Live response queue is full, Buffer#close can block while holding the buffer monitor; Buffer#abort then waits indefinitely for the same lock. Each affected response can retain a web-server thread and a Live thread, creating possible thread exhaustion. The advisory says ActionController::Live streams are affected and large files served through Active Storage proxy mode are exposed to unauthenticated clients.
ai_role: The Rails advisory explicitly says the issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner, identifier ANT-2026-LDFW5N2T. Anthropic’s primary OSS Scanner announcement says its reports are fully model-generated and generated by its strongest models, including Claude Mythos; the individual advisory does not identify the model or scanner workflow version.
classification_note: The maintainer published GHSA-rwvh-fw6r-pwvp on 2026-11-04 and lists CVE-2026-126072. This record reflects the advisory’s conditional application exposure and does not claim exploitation.
remediation_note: The advisory lists Action Pack 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 as patched and supplies patches. Applicability is limited to apps using ActionController::Live/streaming; the advisory names unauthenticated exposure for large Active Storage proxy downloads.

title: Rails Action View highlight can turn attacker-controlled text into HTML attributes
summary: ActionView::Helpers::TextHelper#highlight inserts a matched phrase into a caller-provided :highlighter string without escaping it, then marks the result HTML-safe. If an application places a placeholder inside a quoted HTML attribute and highlights attacker-controlled text, the match can escape the attribute and add attributes, potentially causing XSS. The default <mark></mark> highlighter and block form are not affected.
ai_role: The Rails advisory explicitly says the issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner, identifier ANT-2026-THHUJQVO. Anthropic’s primary OSS Scanner announcement says its reports are fully model-generated and generated by its strongest models, including Claude Mythos; the individual advisory does not identify the model or scanner workflow version.
classification_note: The maintainer published GHSA-v6rj-xm57-3p59 on 2026-11-04 and lists CVE-2026-126078. The advisory conditions impact on a custom highlighter and user-controlled text; no exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: The advisory lists Action View 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 as patched and provides patches. A workaround is to use a highlighter that places matched text only in element content, such as the default highlighter.

title: Rails Action View text helpers can reactivate markup inside sanitized attributes
product: Ruby on Rails Action View and rails-html-sanitizer
summary: With the default HTML5 sanitizer on supported CRuby configurations and Nokogiri earlier than 1.19.5, unescaped angle brackets inside sanitized attribute values can become live markup when Action View highlight splits the sanitized HTML on tags or simple_format splits it on blank lines. Applications passing untrusted text to highlight or to simple_format with html_options are affected.
ai_role: The Rails advisory says a human researcher also reported the issue and explicitly says it was also found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner, identifier ANT-2026-RTK47OH0. Anthropic’s primary OSS Scanner announcement says its reports are fully model-generated and generated by its strongest models, including Claude Mythos; the individual advisory does not identify the model or scanner workflow version.
classification_note: The maintainer published GHSA-2p2f-4rq4-gjwc on 2026-11-04 and lists CVE-2026-126079. The advisory documents specific sanitizer, dependency, and helper conditions; no exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: The advisory says the Rails patches require rails-html-sanitizer 1.7.2 or later, which requires Loofah 2.25.3 and Nokogiri 1.19.5; upgrading Nokogiri or using the HTML4 sanitizer are workarounds.

title: Rails Active Storage proxy downloads can retain a server thread after storage errors
summary: When Active Storage serves a file through its proxy controller and a storage error occurs after the response has begun streaming, send_blob_stream can replace the response with a 404/500 while the original ActionController::Live buffer remains open. The request thread can block until process restart; repeated failed downloads may exhaust server threads. The advisory says the condition applies to multi-request streaming storage services with the default Active Storage routes and can be triggered by a file deleted mid-download or another mid-stream storage error.
ai_role: The Rails advisory explicitly says the issue was found by the Anthropic OSS Scanner, identifier ANT-2026-FMPUMYTB. Anthropic’s primary OSS Scanner announcement says its reports are fully model-generated and generated by its strongest models, including Claude Mythos; the individual advisory does not identify the model or scanner workflow version.
classification_note: The maintainer published GHSA-4v2w-w6g6-f8f8 on 2026-11-04 and lists CVE-2026-126071. The advisory establishes conditional thread exhaustion and does not assert exploitation.
remediation_note: The advisory lists Active Storage 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.4.1 as patched and provides patches. The fix re-raises errors after the response commits, closing the stream and releasing the thread; clients receive a truncated body and the exception reaches application error reporting.

title: nvm can expose NVM_AUTH_HEADER to other local users through downloader arguments
summary: When NVM_AUTH_HEADER is configured, nvm passed the credential to curl or wget as a process argument. Other local accounts may read it while nvm downloads from a private mirror. The exposure is limited to shared hosts and to the token permissions; BusyBox wget remains an exception because it cannot use a private config file.
ai_role: The nvm advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner. Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 announcement says the opt-in scanner uses its strongest models, including Claude Mythos, and describes its reports as model-generated. The advisory does not identify the model or case-specific workflow.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-h3c2-g6gc-6cgx on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121745. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm now supplies curl the header on stdin and uses a private temporary WGETRC for GNU Wget. BusyBox wget still exposes the header in process arguments; the vendor advises installing curl on shared hosts when using NVM_AUTH_HEADER.

title: nvm --save can overwrite a file through a symlinked .nvmrc
summary: When nvm use or install runs with --save / -w, its .nvmrc writer followed a symlink and truncated the target file. A repository or archive can supply the symlink, but exploitation requires a user to run the save option in that directory. The maintainer documents this as an independently fixable write primitive, separate from the symlink read flaw CVE-2026-121747.
ai_role: The advisory says the issue was also found independently and earlier by Anthropic OSS Scanner under ANT-2026-G9REVGKT; it separately credits the reporter. Anthropic’s Oct 8 announcement establishes that the scanner uses its strongest models, including Claude Mythos, and generates model-produced reports. Exact model and per-case workflow are unspecified.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-8qjx-8r8m-mpqh on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121746. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 refuses to write through a symlinked .nvmrc when --save / -w is requested.

title: A symlinked .nvmrc can make nvm print a readable file
summary: nvm read .nvmrc through symlinks and could print the target file contents in an invalid-version message or version display. A repository/archive can point .nvmrc at a readable file such as .npmrc; the attacker sees output only where the victim exposes it, such as a CI log or shared terminal. The advisory says this has the same outcome as CVE-2026-94185 through a different symlink mechanism, and is distinct from the separate --save write flaw CVE-2026-121746.
ai_role: The maintainer advisory directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-G9REVGKT) and separately names an independent reporter. Anthropic’s Oct 8 scanner announcement identifies use of its strongest models, including Claude Mythos, and says reports are model-generated. The advisory does not specify which model produced this issue.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-j6ch-mq5c-3h4x on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121747. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 avoids printing the contents of a symlinked .nvmrc; users of the documented bash cd hook must also update that copied hook.

title: A project .npmrc can redirect nvm prefix cleanup to another file
summary: When nvm use --delete-prefix invokes npm config delete, npm reads the project .npmrc first and may edit a user-selected config file. A malicious project can cause a victim’s config file to be rewritten or left world-writable; on a shared machine that can expose file contents or permit another local user to modify it. The advisory says project code does not run and the attacker chooses the target, not written bytes.
ai_role: The nvm advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-WYRTKBQ5). Anthropic’s Oct 8 announcement says the scanner uses its strongest models, including Claude Mythos, and issues model-generated reports; exact model and workflow for this finding are not stated.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-ccgf-7gv4-xg5h on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121748. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 prevents project .npmrc settings from selecting the config file that npm edits during prefix cleanup.

title: A .nvmrc version can be parsed as grep options and expose local file characters
summary: nvm passed a requested version to grep without -e, allowing a version beginning with a hyphen to be parsed as grep options. The documented option combination can make GNU grep search the current directory recursively and follow symlinks; matching characters may then appear in nvm output and configured mirror request/logs. The advisory limits the readable character set and reports testing with GNU grep only; BSD and BusyBox grep were not tested.
ai_role: The advisory explicitly says Anthropic OSS Scanner discovered this case as ANT-2026-EN9DM7WC. Anthropic’s Oct 8 primary announcement establishes the scanner’s model-generated reports and use of its strongest models including Claude Mythos; no case-specific model is named.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-xmxw-6r9w-89gc on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121749. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 passes version patterns to grep with -e.

title: nvm offline install can reuse a tarball that failed checksum verification
summary: A downloaded archive with a checksum mismatch remained in the nvm cache. If a user subsequently runs nvm install --offline for that version before an online retry, nvm may install the rejected archive and run its node/npm binaries. The advisory says an attacker must alter the tarball but not its separate checksum file, such as through a poisoned CDN/cache object; a mirror controlling both is outside the stated threat model.
ai_role: The advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-7NCT51FE). Anthropic’s Oct 8 announcement says the scanner uses its strongest models including Claude Mythos and produces model-generated reports; exact model and workflow are not disclosed for this item.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-262q-c465-prmr on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121750. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 removes archives that fail checksum verification so offline mode cannot install them.

title: nvm can evaluate malicious Node mirror version metadata as shell arithmetic
summary: nvm stored an unvalidated version field from a mirror index as an LTS alias. Later alias resolution evaluated the suffix as shell arithmetic; the advisory says bash and zsh can expand command substitutions there, allowing a malicious or compromised mirror to persist a payload that runs on later local nvm commands. A project .nvmrc path also reaches the function but is treated by the maintainers as hardening because using nvm in an untrusted project directory usually precedes running its code. The advisory explicitly distinguishes this version-field issue from earlier download-path evaluation CVEs.
ai_role: The nvm advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner with two scanner IDs for this one underlying issue; they are not counted as two cases. Anthropic’s Oct 8 announcement establishes the scanner’s use of strongest models including Claude Mythos and model-generated reports. The exact model and reason for two IDs are not specified.
classification_note: The nvm maintainer published GHSA-7prg-rw9c-82h7 on Nov 4, 2026 and lists CVE-2026-121751. Public AI attribution is in the same item-level advisory; Anthropic’s Oct 8, 2026 scanner announcement is the provenance for the AI program, not the date of this case attribution.
remediation_note: nvm 0.41.0 restricts arithmetic to numeric suffixes and drops invalid version rows before aliases are stored.

title: libheif can spend minutes of CPU repeatedly decoding large derived HEIF images
summary: A crafted HEIF image can make a single decode repeatedly construct oversized canvases while retaining only small crops, consuming tens of seconds to minutes of CPU in applications that decode untrusted images. The advisory reports measured reproduction, identifies no known memory-safety impact, and limits the affected range to libheif before 1.23.7.
ai_role: The libheif maintainer advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner under ANT-2026-XHT9G07S. Anthropic’s primary OSS Scanner page says the service scans with its strongest models, and its Oct 8 launch post identifies Claude Mythos among them. The individual advisory does not identify the model used for this report.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-48p4-gj45-w9v6 on 2026-10-26 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-XHT9G07S); no CVE was assigned in the advisory.
remediation_note: A master fix adds a per-decode pixel budget and avoids decoding tiles outside the image; the advisory says release 1.23.7 is expected as the first patched release. The documented impact is CPU exhaustion when untrusted HEIF files are decoded; no memory-safety issue is known.

title: Trilogy#escape can permit unauthenticated SQL injection with multibyte string encodings
summary: Trilogy#escape mishandles strings in Shift_JIS, Windows-31J, Big5, GBK, and GB18030 because a multibyte continuation byte can overlap ASCII syntax. Applications are affected when attackers control the encoding of strings being escaped, or when using unsupported connection encodings. The advisory identifies unauthenticated SQL injection in affected Rails and Rack applications.
ai_role: The primary Trilogy maintainer advisory labels the report AI-assisted and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner as discovering it under ANT-2026-9KOHJMNW. Anthropic’s primary scanner page says it scans with its strongest models; the Oct 8 launch post names Claude Mythos among those models. No item-specific model is stated.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-744p-w4gc-m3gh on 2026-10-29 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-9KOHJMNW); no CVE was assigned in the advisory.
remediation_note: Trilogy 2.13.2 rejects the unsupported legacy connection encodings and fixes escaping. Projects unable to update can enforce encodings for strings passed to escape/query, as described by the advisory.

title: Caddy rewrite can decode file path information twice and bypass path-based restrictions
summary: The rewrite handler inserted a decoded file-matcher remainder without escaping it, after which the rewritten URI was percent-decoded again. On configurations using try_files, split_path, and a rewrite with that remainder, a double-encoded path can bypass an earlier path-based deny matcher and expose static files; reserved characters can also alter the path or query. The advisory demonstrates the behavior and limits applicability to that configuration pattern.
ai_role: The primary Caddy advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner under ANT-2026-32RAL55Q. Anthropic’s primary scanner page describes an AI model-based scanning service and the Oct 8 launch post identifies Claude Mythos among its strongest models. The item-specific model is unspecified.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-69hv-5jfc-mvmv on 2026-11-04 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-32RAL55Q); no CVE was assigned in the advisory.
remediation_note: Caddy 2.11.8 escapes the file-matcher remainder while preserving slashes before parsing the rewritten URI.

title: SoftFileLock stale-lock breaking can remove a live marker after inode reuse
summary: The stale-lock breaker closes its marker after checking the inode and timestamp, allowing a filesystem that immediately reuses inode numbers to make a later live marker appear stale. Another local user able to create files in the lock directory can force the race, unlinking the live marker so two processes enter the same protected section without warning. The advisory reports the race on ext4, xfs and overlayfs over them; tmpfs, btrfs, a single contender and StrictSoftFileLock are not affected.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory says Anthropic OSS Scanner (automated analysis) reported the finding on Oct 15, identifies ANT-2026-KIIS96IX, and says maintainers reviewed it. The public advisory appeared Oct 17. Anthropic’s primary scanner program page establishes model-based scanning; no specific model is identified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainers published GHSA-fq56-3cx3-fjxp on Oct 17, 2026 and explicitly credit Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-KIIS96IX). Their event history records the private scanner report as received Oct 15; that internal report date is not used as the public disclosure or attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep soft locks in a directory other local users cannot write, use tmpfs, or prefer native FileLock where available; StrictSoftFileLock is unaffected. filelock 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

title: A crafted filelock ReadWriteLock database can make every acquire hang
summary: SQLite loads the full schema at each ReadWriteLock acquire, while the timeout only bounds lock waits. Another local account able to place or replace the database file can provide a small crafted schema that stalls acquires while allocating about 1 GB, or makes them loop at full CPU indefinitely. The effect is availability only; the advisory specifies the writable/replacable database-path precondition and affected filelock versions.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly says Anthropic OSS Scanner reported ANT-2026-NFPRHMYJ, gives the finding title and severity, and records maintainers’ review. Its event history says it was split from a group draft into an individual issue. Anthropic’s primary scanner page establishes model-based scanning; the model is unspecified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainers published GHSA-cwqr-hh33-gh44 on Oct 17, 2026 and explicitly credit Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-NFPRHMYJ). Their event history records the private scanner report as received Oct 15; that internal report date is not used as the public disclosure or attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep the lock database and its parent directories writable only by the locking account, and do not share a writable database across accounts. Version 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

title: filelock can adopt a lock protocol directory created by another user
summary: StrictSoftFileLock and SoftReadWriteLock accept an existing protocol directory after checking only that it is a directory, not who owns it. Another local user who creates the derived directory before the lock user’s first acquire can remove claims, admit concurrent holders, redirect lock-user writes, or hold acquire/release beyond its timeout. The advisory identifies the pre-creation condition and affected versions.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory states Anthropic OSS Scanner reported ANT-2026-Q5VK5JEE and logs that four other scanner IDs were moved to separate advisories, so this row maps to one individually described issue. The advisory says maintainers reviewed it. Anthropic’s primary scanner page establishes model-based scanning; the exact model is unspecified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainers published GHSA-9c4x-gm8v-wgc4 on Oct 17, 2026 and explicitly credit Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-Q5VK5JEE). Their event history records the private scanner report as received Oct 15; that internal report date is not used as the public disclosure or attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep lock protocol directories in a location other accounts cannot write. Where a shared directory is necessary, pre-create and verify the protocol tree as the service user. filelock 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

title: filelock ReadWriteLock can follow planted SQLite side files and alter lock-user files
summary: SQLite reopens the lock database by name and processes adjacent journal, WAL and shared-memory side files. Another local account able to create or rename entries in the database directory can make the lock user’s ordinary lock operation write attacker-chosen bytes to the lock user’s files, create or unlink files, admit conflicting readers/writers, or kill a holder. The advisory narrows affected versions and describes how sticky directories reduce but do not remove all denial-of-service variants.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner with ANT-2026-KMJ2575J and gives the per-finding issue description. It records the scanner report date and maintainers’ review. Anthropic’s primary scanner page establishes model-based scanning; no model is identified for this case.
classification_note: The filelock maintainers published GHSA-v4x8-3wr5-3wq8 on Oct 17, 2026 and explicitly credit Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-KMJ2575J). Their event history records the private scanner report as received Oct 15; that internal report date is not used as the public disclosure or attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep the lock database in a directory only the locking account or root can write, and do not share a writable database across accounts. Version 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

title: StrictSoftFileLock claim directories can let another user remove a live hold
summary: StrictSoftFileLock creates the directories containing claim files with bare mkdir calls, so a permissive umask or default ACL can leave them writable by another local user despite a restrictive lock-file mode. That user can unlink the 0600 claims; a later contender then enters while the original holder believes it still holds the lock. The advisory documents the required permission settings and says the common 022 umask without permissive ACLs does not allow the unlink.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (automated analysis) with finding ANT-2026-AD6SUOON, provides a reproducer, records maintainer review, and states that this issue was split from a grouped draft into its own advisory. The report was received Oct 15; the public advisory was published Oct 17. Anthropic’s scanner page establishes AI-model provenance; exact model is unspecified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainer published GHSA-6627-m3xw-93mp on Oct 17, 2026 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-AD6SUOON). The internal scanner report was received Oct 15; that report date is retained in evidence and is not used as public attribution date.
remediation_note: filelock 4.2.1 fixes the issue. Use restrictive umask, avoid default ACLs that grant other users write access to claim directories, and keep strict locks in directories other accounts cannot write. Existing .filelock trees may need permission correction after upgrade.

title: StrictSoftFileLock can follow a symlink swapped in after its directory check
summary: StrictSoftFileLock checks the coordination directory with lstat, then later uses the path by name. Another local user able to rename the directory can exchange it for a symlink between those operations, causing the lock-user process to create claim files in a directory the attacker chooses. This can strand claims that deny another strict lock or make multiple holders enter a critical section. The advisory limits the issue to POSIX-style conditions and lists the relevant shared-directory and pre-created-link cases.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (automated analysis) with finding ANT-2026-SVFEYX89, provides a scanner reproducer, records maintainer review, and states this was split from the grouped advisory. The report was received Oct 15; the public advisory was published Oct 17. Anthropic’s scanner page establishes AI-model provenance; exact model is unspecified.
classification_note: The filelock maintainer published GHSA-m462-7rxw-wvpg on Oct 17, 2026 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-SVFEYX89). The internal scanner report was received Oct 15; that report date is retained in evidence and is not used as public attribution date.
remediation_note: Keep strict locks in directories other users cannot write. In sticky shared directories, create and verify the lock directory as the service account before other users can claim it. Version 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

title: SoftFileLock symlink swapping can disclose whether a private path exists or is writable
summary: During SoftFileLock acquire, the writability check first uses lstat and then os.access, which follows symlinks. A local user able to change entries in the lock directory can swap a marker for a symlink between these calls. The different acquire outcomes reveal one bit indicating whether a chosen path exists or is writable by the lock user; the lock does not open, create, or modify the target through the symlink. Linux fs.protected_symlinks blocks the leak in a sticky world-writable directory such as /tmp, but not in a writable non-sticky or sticky group-writable directory.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory says Anthropic OSS Scanner reported this privately as ANT-2026-RQ91AXTW, includes the reproducer and maintainer review, and assigns CVE-2026-112912. The advisory was publicly published Oct 17; Anthropic’s scanner page establishes model-based scanner provenance. No model is specified.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-9j6q-wvj5-jgjg on 2026-10-17 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-RQ91AXTW). For filelock, the source records private scanner report receipt on Oct 15; the public advisory attribution date remains Oct 17.
remediation_note: Use a lock directory writable only by the lock account, or a Linux sticky world-writable directory with fs.protected_symlinks enabled. Do not use soft locks as root in directories other accounts can write. filelock 4.2.1 fixes the issue.

title: SoftReadWriteLock can write through a replaced holder record and block lock operations
summary: SoftReadWriteLock refreshes holder records by reopening a path and writing without checking the opened file type. A different local user who owns or can write the lock’s .rw tree can replace a record with a FIFO, making waiting acquires hang beyond timeout and blocking a holder heartbeat so a second process can enter while the first still believes it holds the lock. Where the OS permits cross-owner hard links, it can also make the lock user overwrite the first roughly 135 bytes of one of its own private files with the holder record. The FIFO issue works on default Linux; the hard-link variant has additional OS policy requirements.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly says Anthropic OSS Scanner reported ANT-2026-AT33VEVC, includes the scanner’s reproducer and maintainer review, and assigns CVE-2026-112934. The advisory was published Oct 17; Anthropic’s scanner page establishes model-based scanner provenance.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-fj95-fr6c-h845 on 2026-10-17 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-AT33VEVC). For filelock, the source records private scanner report receipt on Oct 15; the public advisory attribution date remains Oct 17.
remediation_note: filelock 4.2.1 checks and protects holder-record operations. Keep the lock tree in a directory only the locking account can write, and in sticky shared locations ensure the lock account creates and owns the .rw tree first. Keep fs.protected_hardlinks enabled where supported; this mitigates the hard-link variant but not the FIFO stall.

title: SoftFileLock stale-break restore can follow a swapped symlink and link a private file into the lock directory
summary: During stale-lock recovery, a local user can race a path check and replace the marker path with a symlink; the restore step then follows it and can create a hard link to a file belonging to the lock user inside the lock directory. The attacker can read metadata and retain a name for the file, and a subsequent FileLock open can truncate or change permissions on the linked file. The advisory limits the affected behavior to specific race conditions, platforms and filelock versions; a sticky directory on tested settings is not affected.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner and maps finding ANT-2026-SB29HIAL to this distinct stale-break restore issue. It includes the relevant source behavior and records maintainer review. The advisory was published Oct 17; Anthropic’s scanner page establishes model-based scanner provenance.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-crv4-6mhj-j5jh on 2026-10-17 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-SB29HIAL). For filelock, the source records private scanner report receipt on Oct 15; the public advisory attribution date remains Oct 17.
remediation_note: filelock 4.2.1 fixes the stale-break restore path. Keep soft locks out of directories other local users can write without the sticky bit, and do not take a native FileLock on a path another user controls.

title: WindowsFileLock ignores mode and inherits access from its parent directory ACL
summary: On Windows, filelock does not apply the mode argument as a security descriptor when creating FileLock files or the ReadWriteLock SQLite database. In a directory whose inheritable ACL grants other local accounts access to new files, those accounts can read holder metadata, write lock state where permitted, or take the byte-range lock and make the owner wait or time out. The maintainers independently confirmed this on Windows with two local accounts; Unix is not affected and cooperating-process mutual exclusion remains.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner with finding ANT-2026-0KEO0DDO, records that maintainers confirmed the Windows behavior with two local accounts, and assigns CVE-2026-112910. The public advisory appeared Oct 17; Anthropic’s scanner page establishes model-based scanner provenance.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-8mx5-7m5m-r77g on 2026-10-17 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-0KEO0DDO). For filelock, the source records private scanner report receipt on Oct 15; the public advisory attribution date remains Oct 17.
remediation_note: filelock 4.2.1 fixes Windows file creation. On Windows, store lock files and databases in a directory whose ACL already excludes other accounts, or set explicit ACLs after creation; do not rely on mode=0o600.

title: Caddy file_server can expose private TLS keys when its data directory falls back to the working directory
summary: When neither HOME nor XDG_DATA_HOME is set, Caddy places certificates and local CA keys under ./caddy. If a file_server serves the working directory, anonymous clients can download those private keys and use them to impersonate the site or mint certificates trusted by clients that installed the local CA. The advisory limits exposure to deployments that lack both home-directory variables and serve the working directory.
ai_role: The primary Caddy advisory directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner as finding ANT-2026-JBWWW7FF and provides a reproducer and impact description. Anthropic’s primary scanner page establishes model-based scanner provenance. The advisory does not identify the model for this case.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-jf74-f69g-hcj9 on 2026-11-04 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-JBWWW7FF). For filelock, the source records private scanner report receipt on Oct 15; the public advisory attribution date remains Oct 17.
remediation_note: Caddy 2.11.8 hides the absolute data-directory path when AppDataDir is relative, covering Caddyfile, JSON, and file-server command configurations.

title: Caddy host-derived document roots can be escaped through dot segments or slashes in Host or :authority
summary: A site that builds its document root from the request host can let unauthenticated clients choose paths outside the intended tree. HTTP/1 accepts dot-only Host values; HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 accept slash or backslash characters in :authority. Caddy then cleans the expanded root, allowing file_server to expose filesystem files or PHP handlers to execute files outside the intended directory. The advisory limits exposure to catch-all or on-demand TLS sites using a host-derived root; explicitly listed host names are not affected.
ai_role: The primary Caddy advisory directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner as discovering the finding under ANT-2026-YKIEF8GR, and contains a proof of concept, impact, patch, and affected configuration conditions. Anthropic’s primary scanner page establishes model-based scanner provenance; the item advisory does not name a model.
classification_note: The primary maintainer published GHSA-r766-rf9f-588h on 2026-11-04 and directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner (ANT-2026-YKIEF8GR). For filelock, the source records private scanner report receipt on Oct 15; the public advisory attribution date remains Oct 17.
remediation_note: Caddy 2.11.8 validates Host and :authority consistently across protocols and rejects host values that consist only of dots.

title: Caddy file matcher can expose suffix-blocked files through dot-segment paths
product: Caddy (try_files, file_server, php_fastcgi and FrankenPHP php_server configurations)
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: In affected configurations, try_files cleans a request such as /.env/./ into /.env while path matchers still evaluate the original /.env/ path. This can bypass suffix, exact-path, glob or anchored-regex rules before the rewrite and disclose static files such as .env files, backups or configuration. Prefix and */.* rules still block, and nothing is executed.
ai_role: The Caddy advisory explicitly says the issue was discovered by Anthropic's OSS Scanner and supplies scanner identifier ANT-2026-VAGWNYYZ. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but do not identify the model used for this case or the human validation steps.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed vulnerability and scanner attribution; it does not establish exploitation in the wild or zero-day status. No CVE is known, so this record is identified by GHSA.
remediation_note: Fixed in Caddy 2.11.8 by preserving the trailing slash on cleaned candidates so slash-terminated file paths do not match regular files. Deployed patch status is not checked.

title: filelock ReadWriteLock cleanup can recursively delete a directory substituted at its hard-link path
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: On the private hard-link route, filelock recursively removes a remembered `.filelock-*` directory path without confirming that it is still the directory it created. A different local account able to rename entries in a non-sticky shared database directory can substitute a victim-owned directory at that path, causing the lock user's process to delete its contents during cleanup. This route applies to macOS and POSIX setups without a usable /proc/self/fd; stock Linux with /proc mounted is not affected. The advisory also documents a dead-owner sweep variant under specified conditions.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly maps the Anthropic OSS Scanner report ANT-2026-LSSZIUEO to this finding. The advisory includes the scanner reproducer and records maintainer review. Anthropic's program sources establish model-based scanning; no model is identified for this item.
classification_note: The advisory establishes a publicly disclosed, AI-scanner-reported issue. It is conditional on another local account's rename permissions and affected filesystem route; stock Linux with /proc mounted is excluded. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: Fixed in filelock 4.2.1. The advisory discusses hard-link cleanup and stale-link sweep behavior; deployment status is not checked.

title: Unparseable AVC SPS can cause an out-of-bounds read in OpenH264
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: The AVC coded-size scanner discarded SPS parsing errors, allowing malformed dimensions or cropping offsets to reach OpenH264. Decoding an untrusted AVC-coded HEIF can cause an out-of-bounds read, crash, or disclose mapped process memory through returned image planes or thumbnails.
ai_role: The item-level libheif advisory explicitly attributes discovery to Anthropic's OSS Scanner as ANT-2026-W4QT31RS. The release notes independently state that all listed security issues were found by the scanner. The Anthropic program sources establish model-based scanning, but no per-case model is identified.
classification_note: The primary advisory establishes a publicly disclosed security finding and direct Anthropic OSS Scanner attribution. No CVE had been assigned in the libheif release notes at the checked time; the distinct GHSA is used. No exploitation or zero-day status is asserted.
remediation_note: Fixed by rejecting unparseable SPS data in AVC/VVC size checks; included in libheif 1.23.7. The affected decoder-plugin configuration and user-controlled decode conditions are described in the advisory. The libheif v1.23.7 security release is dated 2026-10-26; deployed patch status is not checked.

title: AV1 OBU framing mismatch can bypass libheif coded-size limits
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not specified for this finding)
summary: libheif stopped scanning at an unsized AV1 OBU while libaom continued to a later sequence header and frame, bypassing coded-size limits. An untrusted AVIF could trigger excessive memory allocation; the advisory reports about 884 MB for a 718-byte sample and says no memory corruption was observed.
