classification_note: The pypa maintainer advisory publicly identifies an Anthropic OSS Scanner report ID for this individual issue. Anthropic says OSS Scanner sends reports directly from its strongest models; this case has no named model/version. No exploitation or zero-day claim is made.
remediation_note: The fix keeps a variable reference in PS1 so prompt content is expanded as data when rendered. Disable the environment prompt or use trusted prompt values on older versions. The advisory says the follow-up maintainer review identified additional activation paths; the scanner report itself found the prompt interpretation defect. Fixed in virtualenv 21.14.9. Deployed patch status is not checked.

title: Deletion recovery can change a symlink target’s mode
product: virtualenv (Python virtual environment creation and seeding tool)
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (specific model/version not identified in the item-level advisory)
organization: Anthropic and Python Packaging Authority (virtualenv maintainers)
summary: In a deletion error path, virtualenv obtains a symlink’s mode with lstat() but applies it using chmod(), which follows the link. If unlinking fails and the caller can change the target’s mode, a file outside the destination can become more accessible.
ai_role: The item-level pypa advisory credits Anthropic OSS Scanner report ANT-2026-UK90QC27 and provides its reproducer. Anthropic describes its scanner as operating via strongest models; the exact model/version is unspecified.
classification_note: The pypa maintainer advisory publicly identifies an Anthropic OSS Scanner report ID for this individual issue. Anthropic says OSS Scanner sends reports directly from its strongest models; this case has no named model/version. No exploitation or zero-day claim is made.
remediation_note: The fix avoids changing POSIX modes after deletion errors. On Windows, read-only recovery opens the entry without following reparse points and rejects reparse points. Avoid recursively clearing destinations populated by another account on older releases. Requires the unlink error branch and permission to change the target mode. Fixed in virtualenv 21.14.9. Deployed patch status is not checked.

title: Discourse post cooking can restore raw HTML inside a tag after sanitization
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (item-specific model/version not identified)
summary: While cooking a post, Discourse sanitized raw HTML while it was represented by a placeholder, then restored the raw HTML at the placeholder. A crafted placeholder inside a tag could therefore cause attributes to be inserted after the allow-lister had run. The project classified the fix as a security change; the reviewed primary source establishes HTML injection past the sanitizer, without stating a specific exploit outcome.
ai_role: The merged primary Discourse security pull request explicitly says “Discovered by Anthropic’s OSS Scanner” and identifies finding ANT-2026-ENYESJVJ. Anthropic’s OSS Scanner documentation states that findings are generated directly from its strongest models for this fast-track program; the item does not identify a specific model/version.
classification_note: The project’s merged SECURITY pull request identifies a sanitizer-bypass HTML injection, directly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner, and records the fix. No CVE or GHSA appears in the reviewed primary sources, so the public PR #45728 is the case identifier. No JavaScript execution, exploitation, or zero-day claim is made.
remediation_note: Discourse now drops any placeholder that occurs inside a tag, rechecking each substitution so hoisted raw HTML is restored only where text may appear. The change was merged in PR #45728 and backported to release 2026.10 (#45736), with related backports #45739 and #45740. Deployed patch status is not checked.

title: Discourse inline-onebox titles can cause content-amplification denial of service
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not identified for this finding)
summary: An attacker-controlled or untrusted remote page can supply a very long title that Discourse processes and inserts through inline oneboxing. The primary project release note describes this as content-amplification denial of service; the fix bounds normalized titles to 500 characters before caching or insertion into cooked posts. The source does not specify an exact network-level exploit scenario beyond remote metadata and resource exhaustion.
ai_role: The official Discourse release changelog identifies the original security change (#45745, backported as #45747) as discovered by Anthropic OSS Scanner under finding ANT-2026-Y93QBLJB. Anthropic’s OSS Scanner documentation states fast-track reports come directly from its strongest models; no item-level model/version is given.
classification_note: The project’s primary security change labels this a content-amplification DoS and directly attributes discovery to Anthropic OSS Scanner. No CVE/GHSA was found in reviewed primary sources; use PR #45745 as the public issue identifier. No exploitation or zero-day claim is made.
remediation_note: The fix truncates normalized remote inline-onebox titles to 500 characters before caching or inserting into cooked posts. The change was backported to release 2026.9 (#45747), 2026.10 (#45749), and 2026.7 (#45748). Deployed patch status is not checked.

title: Discourse topic moves can bypass destination-category visibility checks
product: Discourse topic and message category-move authorization
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (model not identified for this finding)
summary: The project’s security fix makes topic moves into a destination category require that the user can see that category. The change applies to moderators and members, and also to converting a message to a public topic or changing a queued topic category; existing admin and moderator exceptions for visible categories are preserved. The source does not detail a particular data exposure or attacker scenario, so impact is limited here to the authorization boundary bypass described by the maintainers.
ai_role: The official Discourse release changelog identifies the main security change (#45852, backported as #45854) as discovered by Anthropic OSS Scanner under ANT-2026-ADPDEAPP. Anthropic’s scanner documentation says its fast-track reports are generated directly by its strongest models; the specific model/version is not identified.
classification_note: The project classifies the change as a security fix and explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner. No CVE/GHSA is named in the reviewed primary sources; the original pull request #45852 is the public issue identifier. No exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: Category changes now require the user to see the destination category across direct topic moves, message-to-topic conversion, and queued-topic edits, while preserving documented admin/moderator permissions for categories they can see. The change was backported to releases 2026.10 (#45854), 2026.9 (#45855), and 2026.7 (#45856). Deployed patch status is not checked.

title: filelock SoftReadWriteLock can follow a substituted lock tree and write outside its directory
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner; exact model/version not identified for this finding
summary: After a lock object validates its .rw tree once, another local account with write access to the parent can replace a nested gen or holders directory with a symlink. Later lock operations then create, replace, or delete the lock user’s own protocol files under another path, including a private Git repository. The advisory demonstrates replacement of .git/HEAD causing git status to fail. This requires a long-lived lock object and a writable shared parent; in a sticky directory such as /tmp, the attacker must plant the lock tree before the victim first acquires it. The documented reproducer ran on Linux; equivalent path behavior is described for POSIX and Windows junctions.
ai_role: The primary filelock advisory explicitly says Anthropic’s OSS Scanner reported this exact finding as ANT-2026-WXXRI4M4, includes the scanner reproducer, and notes maintainer review. Anthropic’s official OSS Scanner description says enrolled repositories receive periodic security scans by its strongest models. The specific model is not named.
classification_note: The public advisory rates the issue Low (CVSS 3.3) and classifies it as conditional security. A different local account needs write access to the lock parent; a long-lived lock object must perform multiple acquisitions. The scanner had reported it privately on Oct 15; the public attribution is dated to the advisory publication Oct 17.
remediation_note: Fixed in filelock 4.2.1. The advisory recommends protecting every ancestor of the lock path from replacement by another account; a sticky shared parent can suffice if the lock tree was not planted beforehand. Deployment status is not checked.

title: Apache httpd mod_http2 assign_headers heap corruption and potential remote code execution
product: Apache HTTP Server mod_http2 and standalone mod_h2
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner; exact model/version not identified for this finding
organization: Anthropic and Apache HTTP Server Project; Google Cloud Vulnerability Research independently reported later
summary: A concurrent-access flaw in mod_http2 assign_headers() can corrupt heap state and lead to remote code execution. The upstream Apache advisory identifies affected httpd versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 and standalone mod_h2 versions 2.0.8 through 2.0.42. Apache credits Anthropic’s OSS Scanner report ANT-2026-MAPKT6MZ as first reported to its security team on Oct 26, 2026, then separately credits Anthony Weems and Simon Scannell of Google Cloud Vulnerability Research for a Nov 3 report. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim is made.
ai_role: Apache’s primary vulnerability ledger explicitly credits Anthropic OSS Scanner as finder of this CVE under ANT-2026-MAPKT6MZ and dates its security-team report before the independent Google report. The official Anthropic OSS Scanner page identifies the service as periodic security scans by Anthropic’s strongest models. Specific model and internal steps for this finding are not public.
classification_note: Apache published the security entry and fix with httpd 2.4.71 on Nov 11, 2026. Anthropic reported privately on Oct 26; Apache publicly names that attribution in the release advisory. Apache labels the issue critical and says it can lead to RCE; no claim of exploitation is made.
remediation_note: Apache fixed the issue in httpd 2.4.71 by updating mod_http2 assign_headers() to write into the request headers table. Upgrade to Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 or the vendor’s fixed package; deployments should also check standalone mod_h2 releases. Deployment status is not checked.

title: LibreOffice dBASE index import heap buffer overflow and recursive-page handling flaw
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; separately reported by an anonymous TrendAI Zero Day Initiative participant
summary: When reading a dBASE index page, LibreOffice did not constrain the recorded entry count to the page capacity; crafted pages could trigger a heap buffer overflow. A page could also refer to itself and recurse without end. LibreOffice credits Claude and says Anthropic found the issue using agents studying open-source project security; Ada Logics validated and reported it. A separate anonymous TrendAI ZDI reporter is also credited.
ai_role: The primary LibreOffice security advisory states “found by Anthropic using agents to study the security of open-source projects” and credits Claude; it says Ada Logics validated and reported. It separately acknowledges an anonymous TrendAI ZDI report, so AI discovery credit applies as one credited discovery among independent reports.
classification_note: The official LibreOffice advisory announced the vulnerability on Nov 5, 2026 and credits Claude/Anthropic. No claim of exploitation is made.
remediation_note: Fixed in LibreOffice 26.2.6 and 26.8.1. The project recommends upgrading to either fixed branch. Deployment status is not checked.

title: Xen grant-copy cache validation flaws permit cross-domain arbitrary memory read and write
organization: Anthropic and Xen Project; validated by Ada Logics; independently reported by CodeAnt AI Security Research Team
summary: Incorrect revalidation of cached grant-copy details can mix frame numbers and grant references (CVE-2026-102703), or place the check restricting frame-number copies to caller-owned memory incorrectly (CVE-2026-102704). Xen’s primary advisory says a malicious guest can read and write arbitrary memory belonging to other domains, including Dom0. The two CVEs are separately identified manifestations in one XSA-523 underlying grant-copy cache-validation issue, so this record counts the shared discovery once.
ai_role: The signed primary Xen advisory explicitly says the issue was discovered by Anthropic using Claude, then validated by Stephan Lipp of Ada Logics; it also notes an independent report by CodeAnt AI Security Research Team.
classification_note: XSA-523 was publicly released Nov 3, 2026. The advisory explicitly separates the two CVE manifestations but presents them as one grant-copy validation issue; they are grouped here as one distinct discovery. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim is made.
remediation_note: Apply the appropriate attached XSA-523 patches to the relevant Xen stable branch. The advisory lists no known mitigation. Deployment status is not checked.

title: Pillow JPEG draft scaling leaves unchecked lossless output geometry and overflows decode buffer
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; python-pillow maintainers
summary: Pillow’s JPEG draft/thumbnail path sizes a row buffer for a downscaled image. With lossless SOF3 JPEG supported by libjpeg-turbo 3.x, the decoder ignores the requested scaling and returns full-width scanlines; Pillow does not verify the actual output geometry before decoding. The scanline write therefore exceeds the heap buffer. The advisory reports attacker-controlled overflow bytes, but does not establish arbitrary code execution. It affects paths using draft before load; decoder builds against libjpeg-turbo 2.x or IJG libjpeg reject this format before the bug.
ai_role: The primary Pillow security advisory explicitly states the issue was found by Anthropic using Claude to study open-source software and manually validated by Ada Logics. The model version is not identified.
classification_note: The advisory was publicly published Oct 17, 2026, and specifies a 90-day coordinated disclosure window. It rates the issue High. No exploitation claim is made; the reported overflow primitive is not summarized as RCE.
remediation_note: Fixed in Pillow 13.0.0. The advisory notes that loading before thumbnailing or setting reducing_gap=None avoids the affected draft path; builds against libjpeg-turbo 2.x or IJG libjpeg are not affected. Upgrade to the fixed Pillow release. Deployment status is not checked.

title: Zephyr RTIO syscall verifier reverses user-buffer memory permission checks
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; Zephyr Project maintainers
summary: In `rtio_vrfy_sqe()`, permission-check results from `K_SYSCALL_MEMORY()` were accumulated with the wrong polarity. On builds with CONFIG_USERSPACE and CONFIG_RTIO, an unprivileged user-mode thread with an RTIO context and iodev grant could supply a pointer to kernel memory; the verifier accepted it and a driver dereferenced it in supervisor mode. The advisory describes arbitrary kernel reads through TX, writes through RX, or a kernel fault.
ai_role: The primary Zephyr advisory explicitly says Claude, Anthropic’s AI assistant, discovered the vulnerability; Ada Logics performed manual triage and report writing with Anthropic Research.
classification_note: The public GHSA was published Nov 4, after the stated Nov 2 embargo. It rates the issue High. Exploitability requires a user-mode thread already granted RTIO access and an image built with CONFIG_USERSPACE and CONFIG_RTIO. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim is made.
remediation_note: Fixed in Zephyr 4.3.2 and 4.5.0, with backports merged for v4.4, v4.3 and v3.7 branches. The advisory recommends rejecting nonzero K_SYSCALL_MEMORY results and checking TXRX transmit buffers read-only. Deployment status is not checked.

title: Mastodon statistics endpoints compute expensive queries before enforcing admin authorization
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; Mastodon maintainers
summary: An instance statistics endpoint intended for administrators performed expensive statistics computation before checking that the requester had the required permission. Anonymous requests could therefore trigger long-running SQL queries and quickly exhaust server resources. The advisory states this is a denial-of-service issue and provides fixed release versions.
ai_role: The primary Mastodon GHSA explicitly attributes discovery to Claude, Anthropic’s AI assistant, and states Ada Logics manually triaged and wrote the report in collaboration with Anthropic Research.
classification_note: The project published the GHSA Jul 27, 2026; severity High (CVSS 7.5). The issue is anonymous request-driven resource consumption; no exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: Fixed in Mastodon 4.4.21, 4.5.14, 4.6.4 and 4.7.0-alpha.2. Upgrade to a fixed release. Deployment status is not checked.

title: Gitea pre-receive hook reuses a branch permission check across refs in one push
organization: Anthropic Research and Doyensec; Gitea maintainers
summary: Gitea caches a positive permission check for one branch and reuses it while processing later refs in the same multi-ref push. A user with a legitimate per-branch maintainer-edit grant could include another protected ref and have the stale authorization reused, allowing writes beyond the granted branch, including protected branches and tags. The advisory reports this on Gitea 1.25.5.
ai_role: The primary Gitea advisory states Claude found the initial bug and wrote the exploit where applicable; a Doyensec researcher reviewed and personally confirmed the reproduction.
classification_note: The advisory was republished at the project’s request on Jun 21; it explicitly preserves the original private-submission timeline beginning Apr 16 for the coordinated-disclosure window. It identifies 1.25.5 as affected and 1.26.3 as patched.
remediation_note: The advisory recommends evaluating CanMaintainerWriteToBranch for every ref rather than caching the result across the push batch. Fixed version listed: Gitea 1.26.3. Deployment status is not checked.

title: PrestaShop back-office listing filter names allow SQL injection beyond employee permissions
summary: Back-office listing filter names were insufficiently validated before being incorporated into database queries. A logged-in employee could submit a crafted filter name to read data outside their profile’s permissions, including employee password hashes and customer and order tables. The advisory states the reporter demonstrated the issue with the most restricted built-in profile.
ai_role: The primary PrestaShop advisory explicitly says Claude (Anthropic) discovered the vulnerability as part of Anthropic’s coordinated disclosure program; Doyensec verified it and reported it to the project.
classification_note: The public advisory has GHSA-whxq-pxj5-qq7v but no CVE assigned. It rates the issue Moderate (CVSS 6.5); exploitation requires a logged-in employee. Older 1.7.x and earlier versions are stated to be end of life and unpatched.
remediation_note: Upgrade supported installations to PrestaShop 9.1.5 or 8.2.8. No workaround is given. The same flawed legacy back-office controller is also present in 1.7.x and earlier, which the project says are end of life and will not be patched.

title: Pillow tiled TIFF decoder reads beyond short tile buffers while unpacking rows
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; python-pillow maintainers
summary: Pillow’s tiled TIFF decoder allocates a tile buffer according to libtiff’s reported tile size, then iterates and unpacks rows as if the buffer held the full worst-case tile. An undersized returned tile can therefore make the `copy4` unpacker read beyond the allocation. A crafted TIFF can crash the process and may cause adjacent heap memory to be copied into decoded pixels.
ai_role: The primary Pillow advisory explicitly says Anthropic found the issue using Claude and Ada Logics helped validate and report it; the report says the data was reviewed manually.
classification_note: The public GHSA rates it Moderate (CVSS 6.5). The advisory describes denial of service and possible adjacent-memory disclosure into decoded pixels; it does not claim code execution.
remediation_note: Fixed in Pillow 13.0.0. Upgrade to a fixed release. Deployment status is not checked.

title: FreeRDP shadow server divides by zero after a client acknowledges a future frame ID
organization: Anthropic and Ada Logics; FreeRDP maintainers
summary: The shadow server stores a client-supplied frame acknowledgment without checking that it is no greater than the last frame sent. A connected viewer can acknowledge a future frame ID; unsigned subtraction wraps, and the next frame calculation divides by zero, terminating the shadow server and disconnecting viewers. The advisory states this affects availability only and, in the default setup, the attacker must already be authenticated as a desktop viewer.
ai_role: The primary FreeRDP advisory explicitly says Anthropic found the issue using Claude and Ada Logics manually validated it. It includes a reproduction and the coordinated disclosure attribution.
classification_note: The advisory is GHSA-6vjv-4hm3-6698 and states no CVE is assigned. It rates the issue Moderate. The default configuration requires an already-authenticated connected desktop viewer. No exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: Fixed in FreeRDP 3.32.0. Upgrade to that release or later. Deployment status is not checked.

title: curl HTTP/2 upload reset triggers use-after-free
product: curl and libcurl HTTP/2 upload handling
ai_system: Claude (reporter credited as “Luna with Claude”; exact model/version not specified)
summary: During an upload, a server RST_STREAM with HTTP_1_1_REQUIRED or REFUSED_STREAM can cause curl to use a freed Curl_easy object. The curl project says remote code execution has been demonstrated only under a long list of strict heap, version, architecture, TLS, parallel-transfer, and timing conditions; the advisory rates it High and does not assert exploitation in the wild.
ai_role: The primary curl advisory credits “Luna with Claude, Anthropic” as the reporter of this exact flaw. The public source establishes Claude-assisted reporting/discovery attribution, but does not describe the model’s internal discovery process or identify a specific model version.
classification_note: Counts as an AI-attributed discovery because the project advisory explicitly credits Luna with Claude as reporter; no claim of autonomous discovery or exploitation in the wild.
remediation_note: Upgrade to curl 8.23.0 or the fixed maintenance releases (8.20.2, 8.16.2, or 8.14.3 in their respective branches), apply the upstream patch, or avoid HTTP/2. Confirm the installed libcurl version because applications may bundle or dynamically link it.

title: Xen grant-table version changes leave stale status-page pointers
summary: A v2→v1→v2 grant-table version change can free and reallocate status pages while retaining previously calculated pointers into the status array. Xen says an unprivileged guest may gain host privileges; information leaks and denial of service are also possible. The issue affects x86 guests allowed to use grant table v2 on multi-vCPU guests; Arm is unaffected.
ai_role: Xen’s signed XSA-517 explicitly says the issue was discovered by Claude Opus and diagnosed as a security issue by Teddy Astie of Vates.
classification_note: One XSA/CVE and one underlying grant-table race finding. No exploitation claim.
remediation_note: Apply the appropriate XSA-517 patch for the supported Xen stable branch. The advisory gives temporary mitigations `gnttab=max-ver:1` on the hypervisor or `max_grant_version=1` in guest configuration. Restricting grant-table v2 avoids this condition but changes guest-visible configuration; use the vendor patch where available.

title: Xen VM entry failure with branch tracing can crash HVM/PVH guests
summary: With branch tracing enabled, a special combination of intercepted #DB, single stepping, and STI/MovSS blocked state can still trigger fatal VM entry failure. Xen says HVM/PVH guest userspace code may crash the guest, causing denial of service. Affected hardware is Intel, VIA, or Zhaoxin VMX; Arm, AMD, and Hygon are not affected, and PV guests cannot exploit it.
ai_role: Xen’s signed XSA-518 explicitly says the issue was discovered by Claude Opus and diagnosed as a security issue by Teddy Astie of Vates.
classification_note: Distinct from XSA-517/CVE-2026-79610: this is a VMX branch-tracing guest denial-of-service condition with a separate patch. No exploitation claim.
remediation_note: Apply the attached XSA-518 patch for Xen 4.17.x through 4.20.x or Xen unstable/4.21.x, as applicable. The advisory lists running only PV guests, or HVM guests only on AMD/Hygon hardware, as mitigations; these change deployment choices and are not substitutes for patching affected Intel/VIA/Zhaoxin systems.

title: Podman image annotation can disable requested container sandboxing
product: Podman container creation from OCI checkpoint images
organization: ADA Logics Ltd; Anthropic; Podman maintainers
summary: Podman treated an image carrying `io.podman.annotations.checkpoint.runtime.name` as a checkpoint and could ignore user-supplied sandbox settings such as `--cap-drop=ALL`, instead applying checkpoint-controlled container settings. The Podman maintainers removed this behavior. The advisory says rootless containers are not affected because they do not support checkpoint/restore.
ai_role: The primary Podman advisory explicitly credits ADA Logics Ltd with discovering this vulnerability using Anthropic’s Claude models. This is item-specific model-assisted discovery attribution; the source does not identify the Claude model/version.
classification_note: Counts once as the single finding tracked by GHSA-2cvf-wqm6-wr9g and CVE-2026-94603. No exploitation claim.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Podman 5.8.8 or 6.1.3 or later. The maintainers reverted checkpoint handling through `podman run`. As an interim safeguard, reject pulled images carrying the checkpoint annotation; rootless containers are not affected according to the advisory.

title: Libreswan IKEv2 EAP state machine null dereference permits unauthenticated DoS
organization: Anthropic; ADA Logics Ltd; Libreswan Project
summary: An inconsistent IKEv2 state-machine fall-through dereferences a null EAP state pointer on an IKE_AUTH packet, even when EAP is not configured. A remote unauthenticated peer can repeatedly trigger daemon crashes and restarts; the project explicitly says remote code execution is not possible.
ai_role: The primary Libreswan security alert credits “Claude by Anthropic, as reported by David Korczynski from ADA Logics Ltd.” This is explicit attribution for this exact CVE; the source does not identify a Claude version or describe the discovery process.
classification_note: One pre-authentication denial-of-service finding. The vendor explicitly rules out remote code execution; no exploitation-in-the-wild claim.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Libreswan 5.3.3 or 5.4.1 or later, depending on branch, or apply the vendor patch. The advisory says malicious unauthenticated IKE_AUTH packets can repeatedly crash/restart `pluto`; verify downstream package versions.

impacts.conditions: A malicious IKE_AUTH packet reaches Libreswan's affected IKEv2 state machine; authentication and configured EAP are not required. Repeated crashes and restarts of pluto can deny service; the CNA explicitly excludes remote code execution.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the cited CNA description; no independent exploitation assessment made.

title: Botan TLS ASIO stream use-after-free may expose heap data
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (service documented to use Anthropic’s strongest Claude models; exact model/version not identified)
summary: A use-after-free in Botan’s TLS ASIO integration can disclose heap data to a peer, depending on the application’s usage pattern. The Botan advisory limits exposure to applications using `botan/asio_stream.h` with simultaneous reads and writes outstanding.
ai_role: The primary Botan advisory credits Anthropic OSS-Scanner under item ID ANT-2026-4PMK7FYH. Anthropic’s official OSS Scanner page says its periodic scans use its strongest models and describes the service as informed by its experience using Claude. The specific model and internal analysis steps for this finding are not public.
classification_note: The vendor release notes say fixed in Botan 3.14.0, dated Nov 4; the linked public vendor handbook that records the scanner credit is dated Nov 6. Scope is limited to ASIO TLS stream applications with concurrent reads/writes.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Botan 3.14.0 or later. Only applications using the ASIO TLS stream API are in scope; applications should review their use of concurrent reads/writes. Botan says disabling TLS 1.2 is only a partial, not complete, countermeasure.

title: Botan TLS 1.3 handshake buffers unbounded dummy ChangeCipherSpec messages
ai_system: Anthropic OSS Scanner (service documented to use Anthropic’s strongest Claude models; exact model/version not identified)
organization: Anthropic; Trail of Bits/OpenAI; Tencent Keen Security Lab; Botan authors
summary: Before a TLS 1.3 server determines whether to downgrade to TLS 1.2, it buffered incoming ChangeCipherSpec messages. An unauthenticated peer could send many dummy CCS messages to pin unbounded memory during the handshake and cause denial of service. Botan’s advisory credits Anthropic OSS-Scanner and also credits Trail of Bits in collaboration with OpenAI and Tencent’s SecBuddyF; the shared underlying bug is counted once.
ai_role: The primary Botan advisory credits Anthropic OSS-Scanner under item ID ANT-2026-5QKEFF4F for this exact TLS 1.3 memory-consumption finding. Anthropic’s official OSS Scanner page describes periodic scans using its strongest models and says the service is informed by its experience using Claude. The specific model and analysis steps are not public. Other organizations are also credited on the same finding, so this record counts the bug once and does not claim exclusive discovery.
classification_note: One TLS 1.3 handshake memory-exhaustion finding with multiple credited research organizations. Botan fixes it in 3.14.0. The public vendor guide with the scanner credit is dated Nov 6; the release notes are dated Nov 4.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Botan 3.14.0 or later. The release notes also describe a configurable limit on consecutive useless TLS records (default 32), but use the fixed release rather than assuming a custom limit mitigates every affected code path.

title: Libreswan FIPS certificate parsing assertion permits pre-authentication daemon DoS
product: Libreswan IKEv1/IKEv2 certificate processing in FIPS mode
summary: In FIPS mode, Libreswan asserts that `CERT_ExtractPublicKey()` returned a key. A malformed X.509 certificate with an invalid public key can make the function return NULL and crash the daemon. An unauthenticated peer can send the CERT payload before authentication and repeatedly cause denial of service. The vendor explicitly says no remote code execution is possible. Exposure requires both the OS and Libreswan to run in FIPS mode and at least one CA certificate to be loaded.
ai_role: The primary Libreswan alert states the project used Claude to audit its codebase and that Claude found this vulnerability; it credits Claude as finder and Guillaume Winter as reporter.
classification_note: Vendor states no RCE and gives exact FIPS/CA-certificate preconditions. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim.
remediation_note: Upgrade to Libreswan 5.3.2 or later, or apply the vendor patch. The only workaround described is disabling FIPS mode, which may violate deployment requirements. Scope requires FIPS mode at both OS and Libreswan and a loaded CA certificate; repeated unauthenticated CERT payloads can crash the daemon.

title: iperf3 server frees streams while remote-triggered worker threads may still use them
organization: Anthropic; ADA Logics Ltd; ESnet iperf maintainers
summary: In the server timer path, stream objects could be freed while per-stream worker threads were still live, allowing a remote heap use-after-free. The fix marks streams done and cancels/joins worker threads before freeing them. The release and fixing commit attribute discovery to Claude/Anthropic and Ada Logics validation/reporting.
ai_role: The primary upstream fixing commit says the issue was “found by Anthropic using agents to study the security of open-source projects,” with Ada Logics validating and reporting. It maps finding ANT-2026-E5BA80X9 directly to CVE-2026-101283.
classification_note: Upstream release errata says CVE labels in the two fix commit messages were interchanged; the fixing commits themselves unambiguously map this server-side use-after-free to CVE-2026-101283 and ANT-2026-E5BA80X9. No exploitation claim.
remediation_note: Upgrade to iperf3 3.22 or later. The patch cancels and joins stream worker threads before freeing their streams. This applies to the affected server code; verify downstream packages include the fix.

title: iperf3 authentication RSA decryption accepts ciphertext longer than its output buffer
organization: Anthropic; ADA Logics Ltd; ESnet iperf maintainers
summary: The RSA authentication decrypt path could process an encrypted input longer than the output buffer sized to the RSA modulus, risking heap buffer overflow. The fix rejects ciphertext lengths greater than the RSA output size rather than continuing with the read. The upstream commit attributes discovery to Anthropic’s agents and reporting/validation to Ada Logics.

title: NSD IP range ACL comparison can allow unintended addresses on little-endian systems

Its timeline states Qifan reported the issue and received a private patch before the later Claude/Ada report; the public advisory appeared only when the fix released. ai_role: The primary NLnet Labs advisory thanks Qifan Zhang, Claude and Ada Logics for discovering and responsibly disclosing this exact vulnerability. Because the record also shows an earlier human report and private patch exchange, this is counted once with no AI-priority or zero-day claim; independence versus private prior knowledge is not independently documented.

title: GitHub gh-aw MCP argument injection can bypass intended command safeguards
product: GitHub gh-aw CLI and MCP server
summary: In gh-aw versions before v0.91.12, MCP handlers appended untrusted client strings into child-process argv without a `--` separator or leading-hyphen rejection. A lower-trust MCP client could inject supported flags to bypass workflow security controls and perform credential-backed GitHub operations. GHSL assigns identifier GHSL-2026-180 and the repository advisory GHSA-f7r8-5pqp-q5p4; no CVE is assigned.
ai_role: The published repository advisory explicitly says Taskflow Agent discovered the issue and GHSL manually verified it. It identifies the AI system and human verification separately; no priority claim is needed.
classification_note: The advisory says the fix was included in v0.91.12 published October 14, 2026; that version is marked pre-release.
remediation_note: Patched in gh-aw v0.91.12, published October 14, 2026 and marked pre-release. The advisory recommends v0.91.12 or later; downstream deployment is not verified.

title: XBOW autonomously discovers Linux SMC-D out-of-bounds write
product: Linux kernel SMC-D DIBS loopback transport
ai_system: XBOW autonomous vulnerability research agents; model not publicly identified
summary: The SMC-D loopback path failed to bounds-check a peer-controlled memory offset before copying data, creating an out-of-bounds write. XBOW says its system handled threat modeling, code auditing, discovery and validation, with humans steering several research decisions and exploit development.
ai_role: XBOW’s first-party case report says it discovered and validated this CVE and autonomously handled threat modeling, code auditing, vulnerability discovery and validation. It explicitly describes three human interventions steering the threat model and exploit strategy, so this is AI-assisted discovery, not autonomous end-to-end work.
classification_note: XBOW reports it disclosed the issue to maintainers before CVE publication; no in-the-wild exploitation is stated.
remediation_note: XBOW’s advisory lists Linux stable fixes; the kernel CVE notice is linked as vendor advisory. Check distribution-specific patch status before assuming a system is fixed.

scenarios:
AV:L - The flaw is only reachable via loopback-ISM (intra-OS DIBS), which requires matching local GID and shared kernel; exploitation is through AF_SMC sendmsg after SMC-D handshake, not remote packet handling on a network-facing stack path.
AC:L - A malicious SMC-D peer can supply crafted CLC dmbe_idx/dmbe_size values and send patterns that drive move_data() with attacker-controlled offset and size; no race or uncontrollable memory layout is required once loopback-ISM is active.
PR:L - Exploitation requires only an unprivileged local account able to open AF_SMC sockets and complete an SMC-D loopback handshake (no CAP_NET_ADMIN or root); the SMC CLC path performs no authentication beyond standard socket access controls.
UI:N - No victim user action is needed when a malicious peer initiates an inbound SMC-D connection to a listening service; the attacker can trigger the OOB write by sending SMC-D data after handshake completion.
S:U - The OOB write corrupts kernel heap memory within the same kernel security authority; successful exploitation yields local privilege escalation, not cross-VM, container-boundary, or IOMMU bypass scope change.
C:H - An out-of-bounds kernel heap write past the folio-allocated DMB buffer can corrupt adjacent kernel objects and be leveraged for arbitrary kernel memory disclosure, not merely a bounded leak or pure crash.
I:H - The unchecked memcpy() allows controlled out-of-bounds writes beyond the registered DMB allocation, enabling heap corruption and potential arbitrary kernel code execution or control-flow hijacking.
A:H - Writing past the allocated DMB folio can immediately corrupt critical kernel structures and cause kernel oops, panic, or hang; heap corruption from the OOB write itself constitutes high availability impact.

title: Google Big Sleep and Grape discover a Blink QualifiedName use-after-free
ai_system: Google Project Big Sleep with Grape variant-analysis mode
summary: A web worker could invoke an experimental Trusted Types parser-options API and concurrently mutate a process-global QualifiedName cache that was designed for main-thread access, causing a heap use-after-free. The issue affected an experimental, not-yet-shipped feature at the time of discovery.
ai_role: The Chromium vulnerability report calls this “a discovery of Project BigSleep (w/ Grape, a variant analysis mode)” and its issue metadata credits Google BigSleep@Grape. A later comment describes a researcher working with the Big Sleep team; the public evidence therefore supports collaborative AI-assisted discovery, not an autonomous-agent-only claim.
classification_note: Google’s release note and issue record establish a fix and disclosure but do not assert in-the-wild exploitation.
remediation_note: Google’s Chrome update fixed the issue in version 151.0.7922.173. The Chromium report says the trigger used an experimental feature not yet shipped at discovery; do not assume it was available to ordinary stable users then. Device update state is not checked.

title: OpenAI Codex Security reports a Node.js Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write
ai_system: OpenAI Codex Security; underlying model not identified in the advisory
summary: Malformed Brotli input could make the bundled Node.js decoder append bytes beyond an internal buffer after it misclassified an invalid block switch. Applications that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli input could suffer a process crash, memory disclosure or remote code execution, depending on exposure.
ai_role: The Node.js security release credits “OpenAI Codex Security - Khai Tran and Sylvie Mayer” specifically for reporting this CVE. Xint’s November 9 response independently reproduces that exact reporter credit; it does not claim Xint discovered the bug. The record attributes discovery to Codex Security, with human reporters/maintainers explicitly credited.
classification_note: The Node.js advisory reports the issue and fixes but makes no claim of exploitation in the wild.
remediation_note: Fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1; restart/redeploy processes after upgrade as required by the Node.js advisory. EOL Node versions may require a distribution or support-vendor patch. Deployment is not verified.

impacts.conditions: An affected Brotli decoder processes a crafted compressed stream; the CNA describes memory disclosure or denial of service, and arbitrary code execution as a potential consequence.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the cited CNA description; no independent exploitation assessment made.

title: Calif and OpenAI AI-assisted research identifies PHP out-of-memory remote code execution
product: PHP runtime request parsing and shutdown paths
ai_system: Calif researchers’ LLM companion; OpenAI attributes GPT-5.6 Sol to Calif’s critical finding (exact model-to-finding mapping not independently detailed in the researcher post)
organization: Calif, OpenAI Patch the Planet, PHP Project
summary: A controllable out-of-memory failure during request parsing could leave PHP request state incompletely initialized; request shutdown could later treat that state as valid, enabling remote code execution under confirmed mod_php conditions. The same underlying issue also has conditional paths on other SAPIs, as described by the maintainer advisory.
ai_role: OpenAI states Calif identified a critical PHP flaw using GPT-5.6 Sol. Calif’s first-party research account describes asking an LLM companion to help find controllable OOM/fatal behavior, then an AI agent tracing an initialization-order defect during source review; this discovery path is mapped here to the PHP maintainer’s CVE-2026-109618 OOM-corruption issue. The mapping between OpenAI’s model attribution and this specific CVE is an inference from the matching OOM description and the researcher timeline; OpenAI’s statement itself does not name the CVE. PHP’s advisory credits multiple reporting teams, so no priority claim is made.
classification_note: Calif reports coordinated disclosure; OpenAI says the coalition prepared fixes before public disclosure. No claim of exploitation in the wild is made here.
remediation_note: PHP fixed in 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12; older branches may depend on distribution/support-vendor backports. The advisory warns that `memory_limit=-1` is only partial mitigation and workers must be restarted after changes. Deployment is not verified.

title: openvt -u could authenticate a privileged login using TTY device ownership instead of process ownership
ai_system: AISLE AI-native analyzer (specific model/version not disclosed)
organization: AISLE in partnership with Red Hat
summary: In a non-default privileged kbrequest/init configuration that invokes openvt -u, the process-owner check follows /proc/<pid>/fd/0 to the TTY device. If TTY ownership has returned to root while an unprivileged process retains that descriptor, openvt can mistake the process for the console owner and start a passwordless root login. Red Hat says this configuration and timing condition are absent from standard deployments.
ai_role: AISLE’s itemized case page says “Discovered by AISLE”; Red Hat’s CNA record credits discovery to Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat. The particular model and division of human and model work are not disclosed.
classification_note: The AISLE page and Red Hat CNA record publish the vulnerability on August 11, 2026. The AISLE page currently shows the finder credit but also an Updated date of September 15; the sources do not establish when the credit first appeared, so the public AI-attribution date is left unknown. This case requires the documented privileged kbrequest/init use of openvt -u and a TTY ownership timing condition; it is not presented as affecting standard deployments.
remediation_note: The upstream kbd commit 78d5ae1 requires both matching process ownership and controlling terminal, rejects root as a pre-authenticated target, and documents the constraint. Red Hat lists fixed errata for several product branches; do not infer that every downstream installation has deployed a fix. Until fixed, Red Hat recommends avoiding openvt -u in privileged kbrequest/init setups or disabling that binding.

title: cockpit-files directory creation owner assignment could follow an attacker-controlled symlink race
ai_system: AISLE AI-native analyzer (specific model/version not disclosed)
organization: AISLE Research, in partnership with Red Hat
summary: A local unprivileged attacker who controls a writable parent directory can race Cockpit Files directory creation with owner assignment, replace the new directory with a symlink, and redirect the privileged chown to another file. The user must trigger the owner-assignment flow, and the attacker must win the race.

Red Hat rates it Moderate and lists RHEL 9 fix as deferred at the CVE page’s update; fixes were later released in cockpit-files 45-1 and Red Hat errata. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim is made.

impacts.conditions: A local unprivileged attacker controls a writable parent directory and wins a symlink race during cockpit-files directory creation and owner assignment; sensitive-file disclosure or modification is a potential consequence.
impacts.exploitation: Not established by the cited CNA description; no independent exploitation assessment made.

title: libstdc++ std::vector<bool> could wrap size calculations and expose inconsistent storage
ai_system: AISLE AI-native analyzer (specific model/version not disclosed)

summary: An attacker-influenced excessively large element count passed to a std::vector<bool> constructor can wrap internal size-to-word calculations. The container may then have inconsistent logical size and storage, leading to out-of-bounds access and application crash or denial of service in subsequent operations. The source does not establish a generally reachable remote attack path; the attacker must influence the count in a program using affected libstdc++.
ai_role: AISLE’s individual CVE page says “Discovered by AISLE”; Red Hat’s CNA page also credits discovery to Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat. Red Hat Bugzilla labels the report AI_ONLY_REPORT. The specific model/version and human/model work division are not disclosed.

title: MRTG root daemon could follow a PID-file symlink and change arbitrary file ownership
ai_system: AISLE AI-native analyzer (specific model/version not disclosed)
organization: AISLE in partnership with Red Hat
summary: When MRTG starts its daemon as root with --daemon --user and then drops privileges, a local low-privilege user who can pre-place a symlink at the PID-file path can redirect the privileged chown to an existing file. This can expose or allow modification of sensitive files. The attack requires the root-started daemon mode and a PID path the attacker can influence.
ai_role: AISLE’s itemized CVE page says “Discovered by AISLE”; Red Hat’s CNA record credits discovery to Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat. classification_note: AISLE’s individual page gives Published August 11, 2026 and says Discovered by AISLE; Red Hat’s public CVE page also gives August 11 as the public date and credits AISLE. Requires local access and MRTG root daemon startup with privilege drop plus attacker control of the PID path. No exploitation-in-the-wild claim is made.
remediation_note: Upstream MRTG commit 30e1921 rejects symlink PID paths, creates PID files atomically with O_EXCL, and changes ownership using the open file handle; Red Hat lists fixed errata for multiple branches. Deployment is not inferred.

title: Cockpit public-key helper could follow home-directory symlinks during privileged ownership changes
ai_system: AISLE AI-native analyzer (specific model/version not disclosed)
organization: AISLE in partnership with Red Hat
summary: A local authenticated user who can control a target account home directory can exploit Cockpit’s privileged Add Public Key helper. Symlinks in .ssh or authorized_keys paths could redirect privileged ownership/mode operations to other files, allowing local privilege escalation or unauthorized file access/modification. The flow requires a privileged Cockpit session, user interaction, and symlink control.
ai_role: AISLE’s itemized CVE page says “Discovered by AISLE”; Red Hat’s CNA page explicitly credits discovery to Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat. The specific model/version and division of human and model work are undisclosed.

remediation_note: Cockpit commit 4796b28 changes the operation to run as the target user where permitted and uses chown --no-dereference for .ssh and authorized_keys, preventing symlink targets from redirecting ownership changes. title: Cockpit do_lastlog offset overflow could misaddress legacy login records on ILP32 systems
ai_system: AISLE AI-native analyzer (specific model/version not disclosed)
organization: AISLE in partnership with Red Hat
summary: On ILP32 (32-bit int/long/pointer) builds using Cockpit’s legacy lastlog update path, a low-privilege authenticated user with a specially provisioned sufficiently large UID can overflow the offset calculation in do_lastlog(). The evidence establishes limited disclosure/tampering of login-accounting metadata, not code execution or privilege escalation.
ai_role: AISLE’s individual CVE page says “Discovered by AISLE”; Red Hat’s CNA record credits discovery to Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat. Red Hat Bugzilla marks the report AI_ONLY_REPORT. The specific model/version and human/model work split are undisclosed.

No released fix status was established in this check; Red Hat Bugzilla includes a proposed checked-offset fix and mitigation guidance.
remediation_note: Red Hat Bugzilla states no released package fix was established at report time and contains a proposed checked-off_t offset fix. Current package fix status was not established in this check.

title: Cockpit cockpit-tls could spawn unbounded detached threads and exhaust resources

title: cockpit-ws could terminate on a request exactly matching configured URL root
ai_system: AISLE AI-native analyzer (specific model/version not disclosed)

summary: When a non-empty WebService.UrlRoot is configured, an unauthenticated remote request to exactly that URL-root prefix without a trailing slash can trigger cockpit-ws termination and deny Cockpit service. ai_role: AISLE’s itemized case page says “Discovered by AISLE”; Red Hat’s primary CNA page explicitly credits discovery to Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat. Model/version and human/model work split are undisclosed.

remediation_note: Red Hat says a code fix is being pursued. Until fixed, avoid non-empty WebService.UrlRoot if feasible or configure a front-end proxy/TLS terminator to normalize the exact prefix to a trailing-slash path before forwarding. No package fix release is claimed.

title: libstdc++ parallel std::search could access past an undersized KMP border table
ai_system: AISLE AI-native analyzer (specific model/version not disclosed)
organization: AISLE in partnership with Red Hat
summary: In libstdc++ parallel mode, the Knuth-Morris-Pratt std::search implementation allocates a border table for N pattern entries but accesses index N. With parallel mode/OpenMP and a compatible consumer using random-access iterators, a full-match search over attacker-influenced data can trigger out-of-bounds access and crash the calling process. The flaw is not established as remotely reachable through GCC itself and is absent from standard builds that do not enable parallel extensions.
ai_role: AISLE’s itemized index lists this exact CVE among cases discovered by its AI-native engine; Red Hat’s CNA record credits discovery to Found by AISLE in partnership with Red Hat. Red Hat Bugzilla labels the report AI_ONLY_REPORT. A specific AISLE case page exists but returned a cache miss during this check. Model/version and human/model division are undisclosed.
classification_note: Red Hat and AISLE public records date this case October 30, 2026, and Red Hat credits AISLE as finder. The vulnerable feature is optional/non-default libstdc++ parallel mode; consumer code must define/use _GLIBCXX_PARALLEL and OpenMP and reach the parallel std::search implementation with data that reaches the full-match path. Demonstrated impact is an out-of-bounds memory access/process crash, not code execution or data disclosure.
remediation_note: GCC upstream commit c1f32b67510f6f9998deadaef5090b6663adb979 increases the KMP border table by one element (N+1), correcting the out-of-bounds access. Red Hat branch-specific package rollout is not inferred from this upstream fix.

title: AISLE finds Cockpit Machines exposes RHSM offline tokens in process arguments
ai_system: AISLE AI-native analyzer (specific model/version not disclosed)
organization: AISLE in partnership with Red Hat
summary: During RHEL image download or token validation, Cockpit Machines serialized the RHSM offline token into JSON and passed it as a command-line argument to a Python helper. title: AISLE identifies FFmpeg LCEVC decoder heap buffer overflow
ai_system: AISLE AI-native engine (specific model/version not disclosed)
summary: The LCEVC decoder did not validate enhancement-output dimensions against the allocated frame. Crafted LCEVC data in an H.264 or HEVC stream with mismatched global configurations could cause heap memory corruption while the stream is decoded.
ai_role: AISLE’s individual case page says “Discovered by AISLE,” and its index defines listed CVEs as discovered by its AI-native engine. The CVE credits Ayoub Nabil Boubagrat as finder and Joshua Rogers (AISLE Research) as reporter; FFmpeg maintainer Michael Niedermayer implemented the fix. The public record names Ayoub Nabil Boubagrat as finder, Joshua Rogers (AISLE Research) as reporter, and Michael Niedermayer as remediation developer; the model and human/AI work split remain unknown, and no priority claim is made. The fix documents a heap out-of-bounds write when decoding attacker-controlled LCEVC-enhanced video; no in-the-wild exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: FFmpeg commit fd6dfa613a48665dcb8d14186b33dad90aa40ae0 validates the LCEVC output picture against the allocated frame and skips unusable output frames. The CVE record affects FFmpeg through 9.0.2; downstream package availability varies and is not asserted for every distributor.

title: AISLE finds ProRes encoder integer overflow leading to heap buffer overwrite
ai_system: AISLE AI-native engine (specific model/version not disclosed)
summary: For very large ProRes frames, 32-bit arithmetic in `ff_prores_kostya_encode_init()` could overflow while calculating the frame-size upper bound. The resulting undersized output packet allowed the encoder to write slice data beyond the allocated packet buffer.
ai_role: AISLE’s itemized CVE index states that its listed cases were discovered by its AI-native engine and includes CVE-2026-125259. The VulnCheck CNA credits Joshua Rogers (AISLE Research) as finder, and the upstream FFmpeg fix says `Found-by: Joshua Rogers (AISLE)`. AISLE’s individual case page was unavailable in this check. The upstream fix reproduces signed overflow under UBSAN and an out-of-array write under ASAN. The vulnerable path requires using the ProRes encoder on sufficiently large frame dimensions; no remote exploitation claim is made.
remediation_note: FFmpeg commit 439b452f9fe916a9f7d8788ab6afee8fac846b0b computes the frame-size upper bound in 64 bits, checks that size against `INT_MAX`, and derives the slice upper bound safely. Downstream package release status varies and is not asserted here.
